berkeley.apis.1.t: Register of the crops of crown lands
berkeley.apis.1.s: Register of the various crops grown on crown lands at Kerkeosiris in 114/113 B.C., with statements of the amounts of rent due the crown.

berkeley.apis.2.t: Register of the crops of crown lands
berkeley.apis.2.s: Register of the various crops on crown lands at Kerkeosiris in 117/116 B.C., with statement of the amounts of rent due to the crown.

berkeley.apis.3.s: Draft of an official letter to Apollonios, epimeletes, concerning affairs reported by Phanesis, village scribe of Koitai, regarding crown tenants of Dinnys.

berkeley.apis.4.s: Register of landholding soldiers who had been granted arable rent-yielding land instead of unusable land, which should then be brought back to cultivation by them

berkeley.apis.5.t: Marriage contract of Philiskos and Apollonia
berkeley.apis.5.s: Marriage contract of Philiskos, son of Apollonios, and Apollonia, alias Kellauthis, daughter of Herakleides
berkeley.apis.5.sup: 2 papyri ; Frag. 1: 29.5 x 21 cm.; Frag. 2: 6 x 2.3 cm.

berkeley.apis.6.t: Official letter from Onnophris to Menches
berkeley.apis.6.s: Onnophris orders Menches to comply with the instructions contained in the included copy of a letter from the Basilikos Grammateus, regarding the administrative processing of a change of ownership of a plot of cleruchic land. The copy of the letter from the Basilikos Grammateus contains copies of all the preceding correspondence.

berkeley.apis.7.s: Maron has leased his plot of cleruchic land to Ptolemaios, son of Apollonios, for three years.

berkeley.apis.8.s: Six lines of probably a private account

berkeley.apis.9.s: Ptolemaios acknowledges having leased to Menches 10 arouras of cleruchic land.

berkeley.apis.10.s: Register of unusable crown land in Kerkeosiris in 114/113 B.C., detailing the reason why the land was unusable and the amounts of rent lost to the crown.

berkeley.apis.11.t: Official letter from Aristippos to Eumelos
berkeley.apis.11.s: Aristippos orders Eumelos to comply with the directions contained in the included letter from Pankrates (overseer of the attribution of land to the catoecic cavalry), regarding the promotion of a holder of cleruchic land.

berkeley.apis.12.s: Short report detailing the situation with regard to the crown land of Kerkeosiris on Nov. 9, 114; text written only a few days latter.

berkeley.apis.13.s: List of 14 persons with an amount of land and dues in kind, whose land had not been reached by the Nile flood.

berkeley.apis.14.s: Register of land with details concerning crops and rents.
berkeley.apis.14.sup: 3 papyri ; Frag. 1: 29.7 x 13.5 cm.; Frag. 2: 6.6 x 18.8 cm.; Frag. 3: 11 x 2 cm.

berkeley.apis.15.s: Official letter to Ptolemaios, epimeletes, concerning affairs reported by Phanesis, village scribe of Koitai.
berkeley.apis.15.sup: 2 papyri ; Frag. 1: 7 x 18.7 cm.; Frag. 2: 12 x 1.8 cm.

berkeley.apis.16.s: Teos, a farmer of crown lands at Kerkeosiris, petitions to Menches, village scribe of the same village, complaining of a raid on his home by a band of marauders, headed by Pyrrhichos.

berkeley.apis.17.s: Portis, a farmer of crown lands, petitions to Menches, village scribe of Kerkeosiris, complaining of a raid on his house by a band of marauders, headed by Pyrrhichos, and reporting which items were stolen on the occasion.

berkeley.apis.18.t: Official letter from Menches to Ptolemaios : draft
berkeley.apis.18.s: Menches, village scribe of Kerkeosiris, informs Ptolemaios, probably the strategos, about damage done to a dike by certain persons who had carried off earth from it for their own use.

berkeley.apis.19.s: List of tenants of crown land who paid rent for their plot in lentils.

berkeley.apis.20.s: Three different accounts, the first (col. I) being a list of persons depositing grains into their private granary account; the second (col. II), a list of figures; and the third (cols. III-V) a list of persons making small payments in kind for crown and cleruchic land.

berkeley.apis.21.s: Two short accounts of payments both in money and kind on behalf of holders of cleruchic land.

berkeley.apis.22.s: List of receipts and expenses for which a certain Melas was responsible

berkeley.apis.23.s: Register of tax payments by 7-aroura holders and receipts

berkeley.apis.24.s: Beginning of an account of payments in kind

berkeley.apis.25.t: Petition to Menches from the Komarches Horos
berkeley.apis.25.s: Horos and the elders of the farmers petition to Menches complaining about an attack that hindered them in their work.

berkeley.apis.26.s: Harphaesis petitions to Menches, complaining of an assault

berkeley.apis.27.s: Certificate that Horos, son of Horos, has performed five days of dike corvee.

berkeley.apis.28.s: Certificate that Orseus, son of Psosneus and Tarm( ), performed his five days of dike corvee.

berkeley.apis.29.s: Certificate that Herakles, son of Horos and Tenapeis, performed his five days of dike corvee.

berkeley.apis.30.s: Certificate that Herakles, son of Horos and Tenapeis, performed his five days of dike corvee.

berkeley.apis.31.s: Nechembes, a tax farmer, petitions to Asklepiades (Nomarches), complaining that owing to damage caused by locusts owners of vineyards had refused to pay their dues to him, which had led to his arrest.

berkeley.apis.32.s: Pherous, village scribe of Boubastos, undertakes to deliver to Bakchios and Poseidonios, both managers of the granary, 350 artabas of wheat within fifteen days.

berkeley.apis.33.t: Receipt for payments in kind : copy
berkeley.apis.33.s: Copy of a receipt for payment of rent and the three-choinix tax for the village of Oxyrhyncha, made by Komoapis son of Onnophris.

berkeley.apis.34.s: Apollonios orders Achilles to transfer payments from fishermen to Onnophris, a priest.

berkeley.apis.35.s: Dionysios, Adamas (both holders of a 30 arouras cleruchic plot) and Poseidonios notify Philon (Archiphylakites) that their house had been entered and property stolen.

berkeley.apis.36.s: Ammonios, a shipping contractor, acknowledges the receipt of 5556 artabas for shipment to Alexandria.

berkeley.apis.37.t: Official letter from Hestieios to Petosiris
berkeley.apis.37.s: Hestieios, village chief, and the crop guards acknowledge the receipt of the kata phyllon geometria.

berkeley.apis.38.t: Official letter from Menches : to Horos
berkeley.apis.38.s: Menches informs Horos, the Basilikos Grammateus, about a strike of crown tenants at Kerkeosiris.

berkeley.apis.39.s: Four columns of an account listing payments made in kind by holders of cleruchic and temple land at Kerkeosiris.
berkeley.apis.39.sup: 2 papyri ; Frag. 1: 29.5 x 22 cm.; Frag. 2: 30 x 17.2 cm.

berkeley.apis.40.s: Beginning of a petition from Apollodoros to Menches, village scribe of Kerkeosiris, regarding the smuggle of oil.

berkeley.apis.41.s: Account of expenses connected with the notary office of Theogonis and Kerkethoeris.
berkeley.apis.41.sup: 8 papyri ; Frag. 1: 18 x 15 cm.; Frag. 2: 13.6 x 10.7 cm.; and smaller.

berkeley.apis.42.t: Petition from the farmers of Crown lands at Oxyrhyncha : draft
berkeley.apis.42.s: Crown tenants at Oxyrhyncha petition to Phanias (Strategos and overseer of the revenues), asking for his protection against possible oppression by other officials.

berkeley.apis.43.s: Senesis petitions to Ptolemaios, oikonomos, complaining that her husband Didymos was trying to give his house as surety to the tax farmer Herakleides, although it was hypothecated for Senesis' dowry.

berkeley.apis.44.t: Official letter from Ptolemaios : to Adamas
berkeley.apis.44.s: Official letter from Ptolemaios, probably the Oikonomos, to Adamas, manager of the granary, of unclear contents.

berkeley.apis.45.s: Asklepiades, sitologos for cavalry dues in the division of Polemon, petitions to Petosiris, village scribe of Oxyrhyncha, complaining about an attack upon him by attendants of the bath.

berkeley.apis.46.s: Official letter reporting certain events relating to security problems in a certain part of the Arsinoite nome.
berkeley.apis.46.sup: 2 papyri ; Frag. 1: 23 x 8.3 cm.; Frag. 2: 28.6 x 10.7 cm.

berkeley.apis.47.s: List of small landholders at an unknown village; the names are classified under headings which include minor officials and persons engaged in other occupations.

berkeley.apis.49.s: Alkimos, collector of the quarter-tax on the salters and general dealers at Oxyrhyncha acknowledges receipt of the contribution (syntaxis) from Androniskos.

berkeley.apis.310.s: Damas asks his sister Artemidora to meet him at the Metropolis (i.e., Arsinoe) at the New Year.

berkeley.apis.311.t: Declaration of priests and revenues of the temple at Tebtunis
berkeley.apis.311.s: List of priests of Soknebtunis exempt from poll-tax, and of payments in money and kind to the temple, some in connection with the sacred crocodiles at Tebtunis; and a list of revenues from property cultivated by the priests.

berkeley.apis.312.s: Petition from Demas to Menches, the village scribe, complaining of a raid on his home by a band of marauders, headed by Pyrrhichus, son of Dionysios, and reporting which items were stolen on the occasion.

berkeley.apis.313.s: A short section of oration of Demosthenes, known from its Latin title as De falsa legatione.
k: Literary papyri, Identified authors; Speeches, addresses, etc.

berkeley.apis.314.s: Known hitherto only in a Latin version, this is a substantial fragment of the lost Greek original of Dictys Cretensis' Ephemeris belli Troiani.

berkeley.apis.315.s: Didymos, also called Louris, acknowledges the receipt of money of 8 1/2 artabas for wheat for the military from the buyer Lysimachos, through the agency of a bank of Kerkesephis.

berkeley.apis.316.s: Diodoros and partners, farmers of the crown tax of Theogonis, acknowledge receipt payments for the crown tax from Aion.

berkeley.apis.317.t: Official letter from Dioskourides and Amenneus
berkeley.apis.317.s: Letter concerns the wrong-doings of a group of komogrammateis (village secretaries) with regard to their duties in the fiscal administration of land. These are detailed in an appended letter (probably P.Tebt.24).

berkeley.apis.318.s: Ponnis and Eutychos, collectors of grain at Tebtunis, acknowledge having received various payments of wheat for various land taxes. Two of the taxpayers are women.

berkeley.apis.319.s: Polemon notifies Menches, the village secretary, of his arrival in Kerkeosiris, and tells Menches to join him to Berenikis

berkeley.apis.320.s: Polemon informs Polemon that a collector had been instructed to stop operations at Kerkeosiris for the moment.

berkeley.apis.321.s: Polemon announces to Menches the approach of a high official and warns Menches to have his accounts in order.

berkeley.apis.322.s: Polemon informs Menches that he sent a certain Harachthes as his substitute to a gathering of village secretaries asking Menches to introduce him and to pay him every attention.

berkeley.apis.323.s: Polemon urges his "brother" Menches to hasten the collection of the taxes.

berkeley.apis.324.s: Pnepheros, farmer of the taxes on beer and natron (salt) of Kerkeosiris, petitions the Basilikos Grammateus asking to be put under his protection; the Basilikos Grammateus subscribed to the petition and forwarded it to Menches

berkeley.apis.325.s: Portions of lines from the 9th and 10th Olympian odes of Pindar.
berkeley.apis.325.sup: 2 papyri ; Frag. 1: 10.8 x 5 cm.; Frag. 2: 2.6 x 1.7 cm.

berkeley.apis.326.s: Two copies of petitions: the first (lines 1-16) is from Phienous, and concerns her ownership of a farmstead at Alexandria; the second (lines 17-19) preserves only the first three lines of a petition of her husband

berkeley.apis.327.s: Petosiris urges Paramonos and the harvest-guards to take care that security for the payment of the rent was exacted from the farmers who had removed their crops.

berkeley.apis.328.s: Possibly relating to the same matter (flax cultivation) as P.Tebt.769 Recto/Verso, the text is too fragmentary and effaced to gain any sense.

berkeley.apis.329.t: Documentary text concerning the purchase of a priestly office
berkeley.apis.329.s: Document regarding the purchase of the priestly office of Prophetes by a copy of a letter ordering the strategos (civil governor) of the Hermopolite Nome to hand over the office (dated Feb. 9, 123 A.D.) and a copy of the receipt for the full sum paid for the office (6000 drachmae).

berkeley.apis.330.s: Possibly a copy of the official correspondence.

berkeley.apis.331.s: Letter from Dorion to the dioiketes Akousilaos concerning certain he-asses (?) which the writer wished to procure for him.

berkeley.apis.332.s: A fragment of a collection of Alexandrine epigrams, including four elegiac poems of which the 2nd (lines 13-20) is by Alcaeus of Messene (fl. beginning of 2nd century B.C.)
k: Literary papyri, Unidentified authors; Epigrams; Elegiac poems

berkeley.apis.333.s: Sixteen lines now known to be from Euripides' play Hecuba; identified as such by W.S. Barrett. At one time erroneously identified as a prose work.
k: Literary papyri, Identified authors; Plays; Tragedies

berkeley.apis.334.t: Field-by-field register of land at Kerkeosiris
berkeley.apis.334.s: Eight continuous columns of a field-by-field register of land at Kerkeosiris, giving for each plot the geographical relationship to other plots, the name of the landholder and his patronymic, the fiscal category to which the plot belongs, the area, and the rent paid to the crown per aroura if any.

berkeley.apis.335.s: Short rescript (written answer) of the Emperor Gordian, directing that failure to register children should not deprive them of their right to legitimacy.
k: Official legal documents, Roman Period; Rescripts (Roman law)

berkeley.apis.336.s: Possibly a fragment of a grammar; lines 2-6 contain a quotation from the Odyssey, book 18, line 130.

berkeley.apis.337.s: Appears to be part of a dialogue, from a mime.

berkeley.apis.338.s: Petition from Harmiysis, a farmer of crown lands at Kerkeosiris, to Menches, village scribe of the same village, complaining of a raid on his home by Pyrrhichus, son of Dionysius, and other marauders, and reporting that items were stolen on this occasion.

berkeley.apis.339.t: Letter from Harpaesis : to his sister Koupa
berkeley.apis.339.s: Harpaesis informs his sister Koupa on a variety of subjects.
berkeley.apis.339.sup: 3 papyri ; Frag. 1: 14.8 x 8 cm.; Frag. 2: 6.5 x 4.1 cm.; Frag. 3: 8.5 x 2.5 cm.

berkeley.apis.340.s: Conclusion of a petition from Harpochras to probably a strategos.

berkeley.apis.341.s: Haryotes complains of an attack made upon him at the temple of Isis.

berkeley.apis.342.s: Herakles and partner sitologoi (collectors of grain) of Kerkesis acknowledge receipt of wheat to the account of Thermoutharion.

berkeley.apis.343.t: Official letter of Herakleides : to elders of the farmers of Areos Kome
berkeley.apis.343.s: Herakleides complains to the elders of the farmers at Areos Kome for waiting too long regarding steps to be taken against Petesokonouris. Meaning and nature of action is not clear.

berkeley.apis.344.s: Beginning of a copy of a census declaration of Heras, daughter of Lysimachos of Arsinoe, Egypt.
k: Declarations, Roman Period; Census records, Roman Period

berkeley.apis.345.s: Fragment of an illustrated herbal, consisting of a treatise on the medical properties of plants.
berkeley.apis.345.sup: 14 papyri ; Various sizes; the two largest are12.2 x 9.7 cm. and 9.6 x 9.7 cm.
k: Sub-literary papyri; Botanical illustrations; Herbals; Medical works

berkeley.apis.346.s: Fragment of Herodotus Medicus' De Remediis, describing the symptomatology of thirst and its treatment; the text corresponds in part an excerpt of Herodotus Medicus preserved with Oribasius (coll. 30. 6-7) treatment of thirst in case of fever.

berkeley.apis.347.s: Fragments of a work written in non-Homeric hexameters. Possibly from Hesiod's Catalog of women, a work popular in Egypt, as the passage relates to King Minos of Crete, his love for women, and the birth of a child, the Minotaur, whose mother was Pasiphae. Only fragments survive of the catalog of women.
k: Literary papyri, Identified authors; Epic poems

berkeley.apis.348.s: Fragment of Hesiod's Catalog of women (the Tyro passage); lines 2-3 are identical to Homer's Odyssey, Book 2, lines 249-250.
k: Literary papyri, Identified authors; Epic poems; Mythological texts
Literary papyri, Identified authors; Epic poems

berkeley.apis.350.s: Few letters from miscellaneous lines of the Iliad, Book 2, with occasional accents and breathings.
berkeley.apis.350.sup: 4 papyri ; Frag. 1: 7.2 x 4.3 cm.; Frag. 2: 6.6 x 8.5 cm.; Frag. 3: 3.9 x 8.3 cm.; Frag. 4: 1.2 x 6.5 cm.
k: Literary papyri, Identified authors; Epic poems; Diacritical marks

berkeley.apis.351.s: Lines from book 2 of the Iliad. Text, which differs from latter mss., is marked in left margin with the critical signs referring to Aristarchus' commentary on Homer, probably the earliest example of such signs.
k: Literary papyri, Identified authors; Epic poems; Diacritical marks

berkeley.apis.352.s: A petition to a prefect whose name is lost from priests of Soknebtunis with regard to their right to cultivate land at Tebtunis, formerly temple land, but recently converted to crown land
berkeley.apis.352.sup: 3 papyri ; Frag. 1: 23 x 23.2 cm.; Frag. 2: 13.8 x 16.8 cm.; Frag. 3, 5.8 x 6.5 cm.

berkeley.apis.354.s: Lines from Book 2 of the Iliad, with marks of punctuation, alterations, and occasional accents.
k: Literary papyri, Identified authors; Epic poems; Diacritical marks
Literary papyri, Identified authors; Epic poems

berkeley.apis.356.s: Lines from Book 11 of the Iliad. Lines 603-4, and 610 contain striking deviations from the common text.
k: Literary papyri, Identified authors; Epic poems

berkeley.apis.357.s: Fragment from the Iliad, Book 5, with elision marks.
k: Literary papyri, Identified authors; Epic poems; Diacritical marks

berkeley.apis.358.s: Numerous fragments from a roll, about 30 cm. in height, containing Book 2 of the Iliad. The text contains several new readings, including a variant of line 4 thought to have been first accepted, but later rejected, by Aristarchus.
k: Literary papyri, Identified authors; Epic poems

berkeley.apis.359.sup: 4 papyri ; Frag. 1: 10.6 x 6 cm.; Frag. 2: 6.5 x 3.5 cm.; Frag. 3: 5.5 x 5 cm.; Frag. 4: 2.2 x 2.5 cm.
k: Literary papyri, Identified authors; Epic poems
Literary papyri, Identified authors; Epic poems

berkeley.apis.361.s: Fragments from the Odyssey, Book 1; a not very accurate text, with a new line inserted following 92.
k: Literary papyri, Identified authors; Epic poems

berkeley.apis.362.s: Lines from Books 4 and 5 of the Odyssey, representing eccentricities common in Homeric texts from Ptolemaic Egypt.
k: Literary papyri, Identified authors; Epic poems

berkeley.apis.363.s: Fragments of the Odyssey, Book 11, with occasional accents.
k: Literary papyri, Identified authors; Epic poems; Diacritical marks

berkeley.apis.364.s: Fragment from the Odyssey, Book 24, with occasional accents.
k: Literary papyri, Identified authors; Epic poems; Diacritical marks

berkeley.apis.365.s: The petition concerns a nursing contract (lines 7-8) and relates misbehavior from the woman.
berkeley.apis.365.sup: 2 papyri ; Frag. 1: 8.2 x 8.3 cm.; Frag. 2: 2 x 1.5 cm.

berkeley.apis.366.t: Official letter from Horos : to the topogrammateis and komogrammateis of the Arsinoite Nome
berkeley.apis.366.s: Circular letter from the Horos, royal secretary, to the topogrammateis and komogrammateis (local and village secretaries) of the Arsinoite Nome (modern Fayyum, Egypt) containing copies of correspondence from the dioiketes (finance minister) Eirenaios and concerning crop management. The letter includes a long letter censuring a certain Hermias for carelessness in this regard.

berkeley.apis.367.t: Petition from Horos and the elders of the farmers : to Menches
berkeley.apis.367.s: Horos, Komarches of Kerkeosiris, and the elders of the farmers complain to the village scribe Menches about an attack upon them.

berkeley.apis.368.s: Horos, farmer of crown lands at Kerkeosiris, Egypt, petitions Petesouchos, successor to Menches as village secretary of the same village, complaining about the theft of 40 sheep for which he was responsible, by inhabitants of a neighboring village.

berkeley.apis.369.s: Kronion, son of Pakebkis, and three other priests from Tebtunis, Egypt, declare on oath that an applicant for circumcision is of a priestly pedigree and fit for the rite. Three of the four declarants sign the oath.

berkeley.apis.370.s: Details concerning the owners and cultivators of land in the Fayyum, Egypt.

berkeley.apis.371.s: Fragment of a land survey list, from the Fayyum.

berkeley.apis.372.s: Liberalis orders Herakleos to pay 200 drachmas in return for barley.

berkeley.apis.373.s: List of numbers: col. 1, alpha (1) through mu (40), each number written twice; col. 2, omega (800) and sampi (900)

berkeley.apis.374.t: Register of owners of temple and cleruchic lands
berkeley.apis.374.s: A list of holders of temple and cleruchic lands at Kerkeosiris, in the last year of King Ptolemy VIII Euergetes II, written in the 2nd year of the next reign. (Soter II).

berkeley.apis.375.t: Register of owners of temple and cleruchic lands
berkeley.apis.375.s: A list of holders of lands and crops at Kerkeosiris.
berkeley.apis.375.sup: 7 papyri ; various sizes; the whole roll measured ca. 29 x 217 cm.

berkeley.apis.376.s: List of persons, etc., otherwise unidentified.

berkeley.apis.377.s: Fragment of a list of persons, with their parentage and ages, from the Fayyum.

berkeley.apis.378.t: List of persons, and house-property in which they are registered
berkeley.apis.378.s: List of persons and house-property in which they are registered, in the Fayyum, Egypt.

berkeley.apis.379.s: Remains of a list of persons in alphabetical order by first letter (alpha through eta) except lines 2 and 8.

berkeley.apis.380.s: Fragment from a list of tragic poets, giving the names of the poets, their birthplaces and the number of tragedies they composed. None mentioned (Amymon, Democrates, Moschus) was previously known as a tragedian.
berkeley.apis.380.sup: 2 papyri ; Frag. 1: 5.6 x 8 cm.; Frag. 2: 0.5 x 1.5 cm.

berkeley.apis.381.t: Lists of names and amounts in arouras and artabas at Kerkeosiris, Egypt.
berkeley.apis.381.s: Three lists of names, some of which appear also in the text on the recto, and amounts in arouras and artabas.

berkeley.apis.382.s: Two lists of names, written in opposite directions.

berkeley.apis.383.s: Short lists of names, and a column of figures, written at different times by different hands.
berkeley.apis.383.sup: 2 papyri ; Frag. 1: 25 x 22.3 cm.; Frag. 2: 30.5 x 30.4 cm.

berkeley.apis.384.s: This work is possibly part of a medical work.
berkeley.apis.384.sup: 5 papyri ; Frag. 1: 12.7 x 8.8 cm.; and four smaller Frag.s

berkeley.apis.385.s: This text is possibly part of a medical work.
berkeley.apis.385.sup: 7 papyri ; Frag. 1: 9.5 x 22 cm.; Frag. 2: 10.5 x 16.8 cm.; Frag. 3: 9 x 13 cm.; and 4 smaller Frag.s

berkeley.apis.387.s: This fragment is part of a medical work (P.Tebt.II.677)focusing on the practical application of medicine and pharmacology against lung diseases.

berkeley.apis.388.s: Fragments possibly from a philosophical disquisition or dialogue.
berkeley.apis.388.sup: 2 papyri ; Frag. 1: 16.3 x 8.7 cm.; Frag. 2: 5 x 2.5 cm.
k: Literary papyri, Unidentified authors; Philosophical texts

berkeley.apis.389.s: Two columns of an unidentified literary text. Column 2 contains tachygraphical symbols (Greek shorthand) between the lines.

berkeley.apis.390.s: Perhaps the remains of a medical work.
berkeley.apis.390.sup: 8 papyri ; Frag. 1: 6.8 x 5.5 cm.; Frag. 2: 5 x 3.7 cm. and 6 smaller Frag.s
k: Sub-literary papyri, Unidentified authors; Medical works

berkeley.apis.391.s: Fragment possibly from a scientific treatise.

berkeley.apis.392.s: Fragment of a literary work, perhaps a lyrical composition, suggested by a possible reference to an Ithacan bard in line 5.

berkeley.apis.393.s: Twenty eight trochaic tetrameters, possibly an extract from a Middle or New Comedy, possibly by an Alexandrine. The scene is that of a wedding about to take place.
k: Literary papyri, Unidentified authors; Plays; Comedies

berkeley.apis.394.s: Literary work, possibly prose, concerning the labors of Hercules.
k: Literary papyri, Unidentified authors; Prose literature; Mythological texts

berkeley.apis.395.s: Magical amulet against fever addressed to a deity called Kok Kouk Koul and preceded by a magical word repeated with the successive omission of the first and last letters, so as to form an inverted triangle, reading the same across or down one side and up the other. Below triangle are six additional lines.

berkeley.apis.396.s: Marres complains to Menches for not having given a relative of his the special treatment he deserved, and urges him to not repeat such behavior in the future.

berkeley.apis.397.t: Official letter from Marres : to Menches
berkeley.apis.397.s: Official letter from Marres to Menches, forwarding a letter from the Basilikos Grammateus (royal scribe) concerning a change of ownership of a plot of cleruchic land.

berkeley.apis.398.s: A series of medical recipes; a large number of them are for diseases of the eyes.
berkeley.apis.398.sup: 2 papyri ; Frag. 1: 26 x 32.5 cm. Frag. 2: 28.1 x 33 cm.
k: Sub-literary papyri; Prescriptions, Medical; Formulae; Medical works

berkeley.apis.399.s: Fragment of a roll. Contains a medical work focusing on the practical application of medicine and pharmacology against lung diseases. P.Tebt.II.681 is part of this text
berkeley.apis.399.sup: 6 papyri ; Frag. 1: 11 x 5 cm.; Frag. 2: 6.6 x 5.1 cm.; Frag. 3: 3.5 x 5 cm.; and 3 small Frag.s

berkeley.apis.400.t: Application by Menches for the post of Komogrammateus at Kerkeosiris
berkeley.apis.400.s: Menches seeks reappointment as komogrammateus (village secretary) at Kerkeosiris, Egypt, promising to pay a certain amount of grains at the village. A certain Dorion adds 60 artabas to the amount promised by Menches.

berkeley.apis.401.t: Receipt for payment in kind : draft or copy
berkeley.apis.401.s: Acknowledgement by Menches, village scribe of Kerkeosiris, Egypt, stating that he has received from Dorion 161 artabas of grains, and Dorion owes him further payments.

berkeley.apis.402.t: Menches' official letter : to Horos : draft
berkeley.apis.402.s: Draft of a letter from Menches (village scribe of Kerkeosiris) to Horos, probably the royal scribe, in which he reports about an attack upon the son of the village Epistates (superintendent). At the end of the letter follows in the same hand a note from Horos, royal scribe of Kerkeosiris.

berkeley.apis.403.t: Menches' Official letter : to Horos : draft
berkeley.apis.403.s: Draft of an official letter from Menches, village scribe of Kerkeosiris, Egypt, to Horos, royal scribe of Kerkeosiris, informing him that he has taken requested measures regarding a judicial inquiry for murder and seizure of property against Heras, son of Petalos, inhabitant of Kerkeosiris.

berkeley.apis.404.t: Official letter from Menches to Horos
berkeley.apis.404.s: Menches informs Horos that Apollodoros, contractor for the retailing and the tax upon oil at Kerkeosiris, had discovered that oil (a state monopoly) was being smuggled, appending a copy of the petition from the Apollodoros to Menches.

berkeley.apis.405.t: Petition of Menches to the Sovereigns
berkeley.apis.405.s: Menches, village scribe of Kerkeosiris, Egypt, and another person, accused of poisoning a certain Haryotes, but released after a trial, seek the support of the Sovereigns Ptolemy VIII Euergetes II and Cleopatra, in their 53rd year of rule. The last two lines (in different hand) contain a directive from the strategos (civil governor of the Nome).

berkeley.apis.406.s: Two drafts of official letters from Menches to brother-officials. The first (lines 1-13) is addressed to Herodes. The second letter (lines 14-26) is addressed to Ammonios.

berkeley.apis.407.t: Two official letters of Menches : to Horos : drafts
berkeley.apis.407.s: Rough drafts of two official letters from Menches, village secretary of Kerkeosiris, Egypt, to Horos, probably the Basilikos Grammateus. Both letters report on matters related to an attack on Polemon, the Epistates (superintendent) of Kerkeosiris.

berkeley.apis.408.sup: 2 papyri ; Frag. 1: 23.5 x 20.5 cm.; Frag. 2: 12.3 x 6.2 cm.

berkeley.apis.409.t: Official letter from Mousaios: to Menches
berkeley.apis.409.s: Mousaios writes to his 'brother' Menches, probably the village scribe of Kerkeosiris, Egypt, about various grains.

berkeley.apis.410.s: Copy of notification addressed to various officials of four nomes (Aphroditopolite, Heracleopolite, Oxyrhynchite, and Cynopolite) in Egypt, that they are to be visited by Lysimachos, sent out to collect sums owing on account of grain dues. Some matter, now lost, apparently preceded remaining text.
berkeley.apis.410.sup: 2 papyri ; Frag. 1: 11.2 x 3 cm.; Frag. 2: 8.7 x 4.5 cm.

berkeley.apis.411.s: A copy, in the hand of Menches, Komogrammateus (village secretary) of Kerkeosiris, of the indictment of certain officials (most likely village secretaries) from three divisions of the nome concerned with the crops, who have apparently made false reports. Appended is a much mutilated note concerning the decision of the superior official upon the case.

berkeley.apis.412.s: Onnophris leases 2 arouras of temple land to Taorseus for 19 years.

berkeley.apis.413.s: Petition of Onnophris, farmer of crown lands at Oxyrhyncha, Egypt, complaining that the wife of his deceased brother and former partner has falsely accused him of stealing an amount of grains from his brother's property, and that he, in consequence, was disturbed from his land and house.

berkeley.apis.414.s: The strategos (civil governor) orders the Epistates of Tebtunis to send up two persons.

berkeley.apis.415.t: Application for the purchase of a priestly office : copy
berkeley.apis.415.s: Pakebkis, son of Marsisouchos, expresses his desire to buy the office of Prophetes at the temple of Soknebtunis (Tebtunis, Egypt).

berkeley.apis.416.s: Pakebkis petitions Longinus, Decurion of the Arsinoite Nome, about an attack upon him and his brother by a certain Satornilus.

berkeley.apis.417.s: Panesis acknowledges having received 120 drachmas from Dioskoros, to be repaid on demand.

berkeley.apis.418.s: Paopis informs Melanas, village scribe of Tebtunis, Egypt, of the death of his father Psoiphis.

berkeley.apis.419.s: Pasis complains to Menches that his neighbor, against an order from Menches himself, has still damned up the canal by which Pasis waters his plot of crown land, causing a loss of produce.

berkeley.apis.420.s: Letter from Patron, resident of Oxyrhynchite Nome, chiefly dealing with private matters.
berkeley.apis.420.sup: 2 papyri ; Frag. 1: 6.7 x 4.5 cm.; Frag. 2: 11.2 x 3 cm.

berkeley.apis.421.s: Paulinus informs Heron, his son, that the Epistrategos (civil governor) had made inquiries for him and urges him to come at once.

berkeley.apis.422.t: Official letter from Petesouchos : to the chrematistai
berkeley.apis.422.s: Petesouchos, village scribe of Kerkeosiris, petitions the chrematistai (Egyptian judges) for postponement of a pending trail against him.
berkeley.apis.422.sup: 2 papyri ; Frag. 1: 22.7 x 14 cm.; Fargo. 2: 5 x 5.5 cm.

berkeley.apis.423.s: Register of land the revenue of which was set aside for a special, unknown purpose.

berkeley.apis.424.s: Register of land the revenue of which was set aside for a special, unknown purpose. Below it is a royal oath vouching for the correctness of the statement.
berkeley.apis.424.sup: 3 papyri ; Frag. 1: 22 x 18.5 cm.; Frag. 2: 1.5 x 2 cm.; Frag. 3: 1.4 x 0.6 cm.

berkeley.apis.425.t: Petition from Petesouchos to the king and queen of Egypt
berkeley.apis.425.s: Petesouchos complains to the sovereigns of Egypt that he was being disturbed in the possession of his house at Oxyrhyncha by Stratonike, daughter of Ptolemaios, of Krokodilon Polis.

berkeley.apis.426.t: Petition from Petesouchos to the king and queen of Egypt
berkeley.apis.426.s: Petesouchos complains to the sovereigns of Egypt that he was being disturbed in the possession of his house at Oxyrhyncha by Stratonike, daughter of Ptolemaios, of Krokodilon Polis.

berkeley.apis.427.s: Petition from 2 or more farmers of crown land at Kerkeosiris to Menches, complaining of a raid on their home by Pyrrhichos and other marauders and reporting that items were stolen on this occasion

berkeley.apis.428.s: Draft of a petition to the king from a cultivator of flax.

berkeley.apis.429.s: Fragments (beginnings or ends) of lines 140-176, 188-253, 277-301 from book 22 of the Iliad, corresponding with the standard text.
berkeley.apis.429.sup: 4 papyri ; Frag. 1: 21.7 x 12 cm.; Frag. 2: 14.5 x 11.2 cm.; Frag. 3: 16.8 x 4.1 cm.; Frag. 4: 16 x 3.7 cm.

berkeley.apis.430.sup: 4 papyri ; Frag. 1: 5 x 7 cm.; Frag. 2: 3.5 x 6 cm.; 2.5 x 6.5 cm.; Frag. 4: 1.1 x 4 cm.

berkeley.apis.431.s: Contract for the Division of cleruchic land in two plots.

berkeley.apis.432.s: Sublease of 4 arouras of crown land at Tebtunis
berkeley.apis.432.luogo: House at Tebtunis T108 and T110
berkeley.apis.432.sup: 3 papyri ; Frag. 1: 12 x 7.8 cm.; Frag. 2: 7.5 x 11.5 cm.; Frag. 3: 1.5 x 1.8 cm.

berkeley.apis.433.s: Repayment of a loan of 820 drachmas
berkeley.apis.433.sup: 3 papyri ; Frag. 1: 22.7 x 14.3 cm.; and 2 small Frag.s

berkeley.apis.434.s: Remains of three columns of a list of names and amounts in drachmas, generally multiples of 4.
berkeley.apis.434.sup: 2 papyri ; Frag. 1: 22 x 20. 8 cm.; Frag. 2: 1.8 x 1.2 cm.

berkeley.apis.435.sup: 2 papyri ; Frag. 1: 22 x 20. 8 cm.; Frag. 2: 1.8 x 1.2 cm.

berkeley.apis.436.s: One column of an account listing receipts and expenditure in drachmas and obols.

berkeley.apis.437.s: List of persons arranged partly according to occupation.

berkeley.apis.438.s: Order to send up the scribe of the tax collectors.

berkeley.apis.439.s: Chration acknowledges the repayment of a loan of 2448 silver drachmas by Thaesis.

berkeley.apis.440.s: Remains of four columns with a list of persons owing 106 drachmas 2 1/2 obols each, with interlinear notes after each entry giving details about the persons

berkeley.apis.615.s: Account listing expenditure for various purposes.

berkeley.apis.622.s: Letter from the strategos of the division of Polemon (Arsinoite nome) ordering certain payments of grain.

berkeley.apis.623.s: Concerns two geese, which Achilleus wants Chronion to obtain for him.

berkeley.apis.625.s: Receipt for the payment of the suntaximon tax.

berkeley.apis.626.s: A list of 5 persons, with amounts in arouras or artabas.

berkeley.apis.631.sup: 2 papyri ; Frag. 1, 8 x 6.2 cm.; Frag. 2, 0.9 x 0.8 cm.

berkeley.apis.633.s: Conclusion of an official document concerning a statement of grain revenues, perhaps issued by sitologoi.

berkeley.apis.634.s: Three receipts for syntaximon-tax of the 2nd year of Trajan, paid by different people to Lusimachos.

berkeley.apis.635.s: Receipt for rent, apparently paid to the state.

berkeley.apis.644.s: Two receipts, issued apparently to different persons, for various taxes, including charge for guards, and for guard boats, written soon after the 7th year of the Emperor Antininus.

berkeley.apis.645.s: A return of house property, addressed to the keeper of the archives.

berkeley.apis.646.s: Hippolutos urges Akousilaos, dioiketes, to restrain the generosity of the writer's sons.

berkeley.apis.647.s: Account of annona (grain, hay, and wine) rendered by a commission appointed by the senate (of Arsinoe).

berkeley.apis.648.s: Concerns an ass, which is to be branded.

berkeley.apis.651.t: Application for the lease of Crown land

k: Contracts, Roman Period; Leases, Roman Period

berkeley.apis.9404.s: The papyrus appears to be an account for a building project, probably a temple. Workers are assigned to tasks for building "is-chambers", "h3t-chamber, "wsht-chamber", and other jobs of related nature. It is thus likely that the document relates to the account of a temple building project. A few officials are named in the document including the scribe Si-Hathor and the Chamberlain Dedu-Nebu. The format of the document is drawn up like a ledger listing names and numbers. The location of the project is also mentioned as being "in Tjeni."

berkeley.apis.9439.s: Marriage contract between Hor son of Psemminis and Ermous daughter of Ermous. The contract lays out the terms of the dowry and the right of the eldest child produced by the marriage to an inheritance. The dowry is set at "4 kite, equalling 2 staters, equalling silver money, 4 kite again as your bridal gift." The contract also delineates what remains her bridal property. Should divorce occur the husband is obligated to pay to his wife 5 deben, equalling 25 staters.
berkeley.apis.9439.luogo: Northern Kom at Deir el Ballas

berkeley.apis.9440.s: The text of the will deals with the 9 different properties. The will bequeathes these various properties upon the Hor's eldest son Abaa.

duke.apis.32042466.s: Lease of a palm grove from Bakchias (Bacchias), Egypt, written on papyrus. The palm grove has dates on the trees that are ready to ripen. The rent amounts to more than 700 drachmai plus 3 artabai (a measure) of choice Syrian dates and 100 smaller sized baskets of green dates. The measure used is the six-choinikes measure of the interpreter of Bakchias. The lessee stipulates access to a drying place as well as a storage facility free of rent. He will pay the rent in year 44 of Augustus (who actually died in year 43 when the lease was drawn up)

duke.apis.32053988.s: Draft of a petition from Panopolis (modern name: Akhmim), Egypt, written on papyrus. Petition is written by Ammon, the well-known scholastikos, or lawyer, to Flavius Sisinnius katholikos, a high official in Alexandria. Drawn up between Dec. 9 and Dec. 13, 348 A.D. in Alexandria. Ammon claims the three female Phoenician slaves left by his brother Harpokration rhetor and panegyrist in Alexandria. His brother died on a trip through Greece, Rome and Constantinople. Afterwards, Eugeneios, a clerk at the chancellory, claimed the three slaves as having no other legal owner and secured the imperial permission to do so at some expense

duke.apis.32054083.s: Text with a power of attorney from Panopolis (modern name: Akhmim), Egypt, written on papyrus. Aurelius Ammon son of Petearbeschinis, the well-known scholastikos or lawyer, from Panopolis authorizes with this power of attorney his friend Aurelius Faustinos, former magistrate and councillor, of Panopolis to represent him in Alexandria while he is engaged in getting his land sown. The slaves formally owned by his deceased brother Harpokration have been claimed by someone in Alexandria. Ammon wants Faustinus to inform Flavius Nestorius, the praefectus Aegypti or prefect of Egypt, that Ammon is his brother's sole heir. Second frame of glass has a fine linen cloth that was wrapped around P.Duk.inv. 19 when it was rolled up. Verso has a

duke.apis.33867979.t: Account of rent and tax payments in kind [2nd cent. B.C.]
duke.apis.33867979.s: Account of payments of rents and taxes in kind from the Arsinoite Nome (modern name: Fayyum), Egypt, written on papyrus. Payments are made by farmers of state and temple land including land owned by the great god Osorsouchos(?). There are payments in wheat and barley for tax on green fodder, tax on pasturage, a one twenty-fourth tax, and a three-choinikes (a dry measure) tax. Recto has a documentary text in Greek (P.Duk.inv. 1319 R)

michigan.apis.118.s: Pen drawing of Sobk, Souchos, the crocodile god of the Arsinoite nome, in the shape of his sacred animal, lying on a litter, which is placed on top of a large stone platform or altar. In front of the god (to the right of the drawing) a small altar with votive offerings. Souchos is reposing in his shrine, or under some sort of canopy, resting on four columns, with festoons and bunches of flowers(?) hanging from one to another. The roof is adorned by a profile cornice. To the left on the ostracon there is a large blot of ink with a dozen vertical lines mounting from it (lake with reeds?)

michigan.apis.447.t: Delivery of grain from granary to harbor
michigan.apis.447.s: Delivery of 50 sacks (of wheat) is credited to the account of an unnamed village. The work of transporting this amount was spread over a period of almost exactly 6 1/2 months, from Mesore to Mecheir 15, i.e. July 25 - Feb. 9. If the ostracon records the total contribution of the village, it was a very small locality indeed. It is more likely that this short text is a summary memorandum of deliveries made by a single landholder also unamed. Cf. O.Mich. 9926, which covers deliveries made by Doulos, son of Aionis, over a period of more than three months.

michigan.apis.793.s: The prayer on the ostracon was addressed to the Dioscuri precisely in their role of Savior Gods. The text is unfortunately much damaged, but there is little doubt that it was a personal prayer. No other inference is quite reasonable in view of the name Muranos in l. 2. The meaning of the broken text in ll. 1-2 is in all likelihood accurately represented by "save Muranon". Nevertheless, the three-fold invocation has a liturgical flavor.

michigan.apis.1134.s: What remains of this text exhibits no syntactical pattern. The word "zodia" at the end of the first line that is legible, is followed by a series of vowels, six omicrons and six epsilons, in l. 2, and these are followed by the words "gune" and "paidin" in l. 3. The vowels suggest that we have here a piece of magic, and this notion is reinforced by the frequent use elsewhere of "zodia" to designate the crude figures so often seen on magical papyri. The collocation of "gune" and "paidin" is strange, but this oddity falls into place if the text is a set of directions for preparing a magical spell or an amulet. The Greek words then fix the positions relative to the vowels that are to be assigned to the "zodia" and the drawings of a woman and child. If the latter were perchance intended to represent Isis and the young Horus (Harpocrtaes), we might think of an amulet for promoting conception, childbirth, or lacation, although the more general purposes of maintaining domestic harmony or preventing illness would not be excluded.

michigan.apis.1186.s: The amount of text which is preserved, especially after l. 5, is distressingly meager, and the content of the fragment cannot established in detail. The action does come into focus for a moment in lines 3-5: Dionysus is addressing his Bacchantes. In lines 6-7 we see Pan with his reed-pipe in the retinue of Dionysus. In line 10, if the reading proposed is sound, the Bacchantes may be expressing with prostaxon their submission to the god's will. The followers of Bacchus are named Lenaiai, which makrs the fragment as a piece of late composition.

michigan.apis.1191.s: An account of payments in kind expressed in gomoi or "loads", a measure used frequently for chaff, but found also with other products, e. g. wheat, hay, dates, anise, and wood. Since the payment recorded in line 7 follows immediately on a statement of areas, and chaff assessments are known to have been been based on the aroura, the account may very well be concerned with collections of chaff. And if line 5 has been interpreted correctly, the entire account is probably devoted to dues collected from the priestly corporation of a temple.

michigan.apis.1205.t: Declaration of Land for the Census of 302 A. D.
michigan.apis.1205.s: The document contains eleven declarations of land for the census of the year 302 A.D. All are of the same day (Thoth 26), this being the date preserved in five of the eleven columns, with a portion of the date in other columns. The eleven declarations are from Karanis, Arsinoe and Ptolemais Nea, but the plots declared are without exception about the village of Ptolemais Nea. The head of the census is the same Septimius Sabinus who had charge of the work in that none five years earlier (see P.Corn. 19 = P.Corn. inv. no II 30).;The census was instituted in accordance with an imperial decree which was sent abroad over Egypt by order of the catholicos, at that time being Valerius Euethius. The first step was a declaration made by landowners and landholders to the censitor of all the taxable land held by them. In our document the primary declaration had been made a short time before, as appears from the phrase "apo tes apographeises up' emou proen epi Sabeino kensitori". The next move was taken by the goverment officials. The land reported as "chersos" or "adespotos" was checked over by the bureau of the landmeasurer ("anametretes"). In our document this occured in the month Thoth at the height of the flood season. The investigation was designed to determine what amount of the land reported by individuals as "dry" or "ownerless" should actually be classified as seed land ("en spora" or "sporime ge"). The peasant landowner or landlord was held responsible both for correct measurement and for declaration of the gain of the goverment resulting from the substitution of "seed land" for the "dry" and "tenantless" amounts primarily reported.;It is at this point that the action and report envisaged in the present Cornell papyrus. Accompanied by three recognised surveyros ("geometrai"), the peasant owner or tenant had measured the "chersos" and "adespotos" portions of his plots which the goverment had designated as probably transferable to the classification of "basilike ge sporime". Note that in all these cases the landmeasurer had meantime "found" that the land was seed land. Three village officials accompanied the peasant owner or tenant and the three surveyors. These were the boundary official ("oriodeiktes"), the village headman ("meizon tes komes") and the village chief ("komarches"). Upon agreement reached by them the tenant declared under imperial oath the amount of his land which was to be transferred from the classification of ownerless goverment land to the higher production category of "royal seedd land" (with higher rate of rent) or from the category of private dry land to that of private seed land (with corresponding increase in the land tax).;Egypt had been the scene of serious disturbance during the suppression of the revolt of L.Domitius Domitianus (Achilleus) in A.D. 295-296 A.D. In A.D. 302 the situation was so acute that Diocletian diverted a part of the grain which normally went to Rome for the relief of Alexandria. For the census of the year 302 special inducements must have been offred to the peasants to take abandoned goverment land. The nature of these inducements we cannot know. Their results, hoever, are apparent in this census roll.

michigan.apis.1213.s: Granios informs his brother Ignantios that a letter from Pompeianos related to him a series of events in the capital, beginning with the arrival there of Ignatios' horse. The animal was appraised by the prefect at a value of 200 drachmae (=50 staters); the price is not high and the horse was apparently not a valuable animal. At this juncture, according to Pompeianos' letter, Proklos, cavalry and vexillarius, appeared, claimimg that Ignatios owes him 28 staters for fodder. Although the verb "katenguhse{to?}" in l. 11 presents difficulties, it is nevertheless clear that the curator did provide on pledge an advance of 30 staters and that this sum Proklos has now paid toward the price of the horse, in order that he owe but 20 staters remainder against its purchase. The full purchase price to be paid by Proklos is identical with the appraisal of the prefect, and Proklos' eagerness to have this horse may stem from the fact that aestimatio from the prefect indicated that the horse has already been approved for army service. Granios closes his letter by assuring Ignatios that he will not bother to go to Alexandria.

michigan.apis.1217.t: Receipt for rent paid by transfer of bank deposit
michigan.apis.1217.s: A woman named Tasis, resident of Dionysias, which was located in the division of Themistes at the western end of Lake Moeris, has rented a farm plot belonging to her to one Anoubas who lived in the village of Philoteris. The latter village lay some miles to the southeast of Dionysias along the road leading into the Faum from the Small Oasis. In the month Epeiph, sometime between July 14 and 23, Anoubas piad the rent on this plot. Since the receipt was made out by the village bank of Palamedes, the rent must have been paid by the lessee to the bank. Whether both the peasant Anoubas and the lessee Tasis had deposits at this bank, and the rent was paid by a mere transfer of the necessary amount upon the bank's books from one account to the other, or whether the lessee Anoubas brought the actual money and deposited it to the account of Tasis, does not appear from the document. The form of the receipt has a costomary characteristic of the statements of deposit-transfers made out by the Egyptian banks, namely that the usual greeting (xairein) is lacking, and that the fact of the transfer is put in the accusative-infinitive construction without the governing verb. BGU 70 is an example of such a transfer statement and happens to be from the same bank.

michigan.apis.1258.s: Herakleides, the writer was the owner of a farm which contained a palm grove with wines planted beneath the palms. These had reached such a height that the vines growing beneath them were receiving too much shade. Therefore it had become necessary to sacrifice the palms by cutting out the cabbage-like crowns at the top of the trunks. The letter mentions two laborers working on the farm, each with several of his own drafts animals. The farm property of Herakleides must therefore have been of considerable size.

michigan.apis.1278.t: A day-book of tax payments in kind on imperial estates
michigan.apis.1278.s: A register similar to BGU IX 1893, a daybook of the collection of produce by the sitologi of Bernikis Aigialou (near Theadelphia) in A.D. 149, over a period of two and one-half months. After each name, 1in 1893, the place and amount of wheat (barley, beans) are given, and at the end of each day a total id drawn. Wheat, barley and beans are totally separately, but the totals do not distinguish between collections made from the village and those made from imperial estates in the neighborhood. Lines 1-6 of the text contain payments of wheat which were made on the 24th of an unknown month by six individuals who were apparently the lessees of various portions of imperial estates in the neighoorhood of Theadelphia. Lines 7-9 contain the total of wheat for the day with an analysis by estate. The ousiai are the Alexandriane, Germanikiane, Maikenatiane, Pallantos, Senekane.

michigan.apis.1305.s: What exactly the letter is about remains unclear. Dorotheos is evidently in deep trouble and hopes that John will extricate him. However, his concrete problem, as well as the cause thereof, is concealed by a string of complimentary formulas and generalities. In ll. 10-11 the writer finally seems on the verge of divulging the details, but at this point the papyrus unfortunately breaks off. All that is left is the bare mention of a sum of twenty solidi.

michigan.apis.1329.s: The text is clearly a homily. The part that remains begins with a simple list of various evil deeds perpetrated by characters in the Old Testament. Some of these are obscured by mutilations of the text and some by strange spelling of proper names, but for the most part they are easily recognizable. Because of his wickedness, the homilist continues, the devil has gained the upper hand and seks to snare the unwary. But help is at hand through Jesus Christ, who has sown the good seed and multiplied the number of those who believe in him. He has poured upon us the water of baptism and we have received his body and blood. The sins of the world have been pardoned through the gifts of God.

michigan.apis.1330.dt: (Late) Ist century A.D. or (early) IInd century A.D.

michigan.apis.1331.s: Homer, Odyssey 11.577-610 (om. 590, 604). In general the text follows the vulgate. Its divergences are paralleled from other sources, and both omitted lines are missing from a number of other examples of Odussey 11.;579 deitr[on: read "dhtron"; vulg. "dertron". The Michigan reading, with emended spelling, is paralleled in one MS (Parisiensis 2680). The vulgate is the only possible reading of the three found in the MSS. The third is "deltron"; cf. OCT, app. crit., ad loc.;582: "kra]ter: rec. "chalep". The Michigan reading is vulgate and is supported by a substandial majority of the MSS; cf. OCT, app. crit., ad loc. Writing the vulagte here makes the line =593 except for the object of the verb. There is no real choise between the two readings. Didymus (sch. min.) in the lemma reads "kratera";586: possin" the nu-movable is unnecessary.;588: dendrea th": vulg. "dendrea d". The Michigan reading is supported by a number of MSS (cf. OCT, app. crit. ad loc.) as well as by P.Fay. 310. But "de" is necessary to introduce the new sentence.;590 om. The line was omitted in one MS (Venetus 456) but added in margine with an indication that it should be read after 588. It is easy to see how the line might have been omitted; it is superfluous. Lines 586-590 = 8. 114-115; if the omission of 590 is valid, its inclusion in many MSS may have been cause by reminiscence of 8.114-115;591 "ei[thusei: read "ithusei";592 reip]taske: read "riptaske. The width of the lacuna (about 6 letters) makes it necessary to assume etacism here.;604 om. The line has a history of omission. It is missing from a number of MSS (cf. OCT, app. cirt., ad loc.) as well as from P.Fay. 310. Line 604, along with 602 and 603, was athetized by Aristarchus, and it was said to have been interopolated by Onomakritos (schl. H). Line 604 = Hes. Theof. 952.
michigan.apis.1331.sup: 8 papyri ; a: 8.5 x 3 cm; b: 11 x 3.6 cm; c: 1.5 x 1.3 cm; d: 7 x 2.2 cm; e: 9 x 3 cm. Three small scraps entirely illegible: a: 1.3 x 1.1 cm; b: 0.8 x 1.3 cm; c: 5.3 x 1.1 cm

michigan.apis.1335.s: Letter written, with many misspellings, by Antonius to Apuleius and Valerias (his brother and sister-in-law?) about some articles of clothing

michigan.apis.1336.s: Iliad 13.290-301. There are no variations in the text from the vulgate.

michigan.apis.1337.s: Iliad 3.260-270. The small amount of text which survives presents no variant readings

michigan.apis.1338.s: Iliad 2. 745-754. No variation from the standard text

michigan.apis.1339.s: Letter from Valeria (and Thermouthas) to Thermoution, pressing her to take up the rearing of Thermouthas' child

michigan.apis.1340.s: Homer, Odyssey 22.226-241;The text gives one reading which is at variance with the receptus text (233), but which is supported by most MSS and by the vulgate tradition.;231: "ktem[ath": the dot over mu appears to be a simple slip of the pen. It is not meant to cancel the letter.;233: "istaso": rec. "istao". The Michigan reading is vulagte and is supported, e.g. by P.Oxy. III 448 ad loc. But the reading of one MS (Harleianus 5674) of the thirteenth century, istao (present middle imperative) is far superior. An imperative is necessary to parallel the two other imperatives in the line (age, ide). Zenodotus and Aristarchus both read :paristao".;236: et]...[lk]ea: the area between the lacunae is too badly stripped to be read with any confidence. There is space for 3 letters. the receptus text's -era- would fir well.

michigan.apis.1341.s: Contains a copy of a document that registers the payment of a penalty (prostimon) which Heraclas, son of Archelaos, had paid to the public bankers of Oxyrhynchus on April 21, 159.
michigan.apis.1341.luogo: Oxyrhynchite nome, Middle Egypt, province of Egypt

michigan.apis.1342.s: A joint declaration stating that premises in the quarter of Dionysius' Region in Arsinoe belong to them and their brothers, and they declare themselves and their tenants as inhabitants of the said premises.
michigan.apis.1342.luogo: Arsinoe, Arsinoite nome, province of Egypt

michigan.apis.1343.s: This papyrus contains an oracle question directed towards Isis. The author appears to question the oracle about some type of struggle, possibly an illness, since Isis was a goddess of healing.

michigan.apis.1344.s: ll. 2-5 appear to be concerned with Deianeira, whose father Oineus ruled at Calydon, and Heracles' fight with the river Achelous for her
michigan.apis.1344.dt: IVth century A.D. - Vth century A.D.

michigan.apis.1349.luogo: Tebtynis, Polemonos meris, Arsinoite nome, province of Egypt

michigan.apis.1350.s: Demotic contract for the sale of a half share in two rooms, made by Thermouthis, daughter of Marepsemis, to her son, Eutychos the elder; the subscriptions are in Greek, as well as the date which was added at the top of the papyrus

The first contract (recto, col. I-II) is an acknowledgment by Haryotes that he has received from father-in-law Didymos a gift (prosdosis and prosphora) 20 drachmai and 5 arourai of a catoecic allotment, in addition to the dowry given to him four years earlier, presumably at the time of the marriage with Didymos's daughter, Herakleia; in case of divorce Haryotes agrees to restore to Didymos or to Herakleia both the dowry and the additional gift.
michigan.apis.1354.luogo: Tebtynis, Polemonos meris, Arsinoite nome, province of Egypt

P.Mich. V, 341, bears the authentic subscriptions to a contract which must have been produced from this draft, but its body is left unwritten on that papyrus.

V, 350) and from a sixth brother who in the interval had died intestate. The heirs receive approximately equal shares, except for the eldest who receives an extra allotment of six arourai, perhaps as a compensation for the care of his parents in their old age. The property divided amounts to a total of 107 1/2 arourai of catoecic allotments, 5 7/8 arourai of vineyards, and 18 slaves.

The body of the contract is left unfinished; the signalments of Orseus and Nestnephis are given in a note in the left margin.
michigan.apis.1370.luogo: Tebtynis, Polemonos meris, Arsinoite nome, province of Egypt
k: Tebtynis, Polemonos meris, Arsinoite nome; Theogonis; he kyle (koile) legomene; Tali (Talei)

michigan.apis.1372.luogo: Tebtynis, Polemonos meris, Arsinoite nome, province of Egypt

V, 283-284, which might concern the same sale)
michigan.apis.1373.luogo: Tebtynis, Polemonos meris, Arsinoite nome, province of Egypt

michigan.apis.1375.s: unidentified martyrdom that has some points of resemblance to the martyrdom of Cyriacus and Julitta.

michigan.apis.1376.s: The text is the beginning of a private letter from a certain Mena to his father. We only learn from the remaining part of the letter that the writer acknowledges that he has caused his father certain inconveniences and that the brother have been forced to work in the field. It is unclear whether these are relatives of the writer or whether the letter belongs in the context of a monastery.

michigan.apis.1377.s: Petros, writing to Timothea, touches upon irrigation and related topics and includes quotations from a man named Abraham, who will offer assistance. Although the drift of the letter is plain enough, the writer does not mark the transition from Abraham's words to his own.

michigan.apis.1378.s: Letter from Osire (?) to someone further south, who is to get money, keep a part himself, and send the rest to the writer by the writer's messenger, Viktor.

michigan.apis.1379.dt: IInd century A.D. - IIIrd century A.D.

michigan.apis.1380.s: Acknowledgement of receipt of poll tax in the amount of 1 solidus. Chloul, the tax payer, did carpeting worth 1 solidus as a way to meet his tax obligation.
michigan.apis.1380.luogo: Hermopolite nome, Middle Egypt, provinceof Egypt

michigan.apis.1381.s: This text appears to be a business letter involving cattle and camels. The address, on the recto, is illegible and much ligatured.

michigan.apis.1383.s: Hypothesis to Iliad Books 10-17. Scholia Minora; Paraphrase of the Iliad

michigan.apis.1384.t: Either a commenatry on a poem, with an excursus on the arrangement of the work as a whole, or a continuous monograph on oikonomia (illustrated with specific examples).
michigan.apis.1384.s: A commentary on the Argonaut story or a treatise on literary criticism. Several episodes from that the story (none of which is found in Apollonius of Rhodes) are discussed, among them Heracles' rescue of Hesione (with a citation of Dionysius Scytobrachion, lines 5-8) and Aphrodite's intervention with Aietes (line 23? known from Naupactia). Although both Dionysius and Apollonius are mentioned by name, it seems unlikely that either is the main subject of the text. Lines 9-17 evidently contained an estimate of the arrangement (oikonomia) of a work (presumably on the Argonauts), but here too the prcise subject is unclear, and perhaps there is a comparison between two works.

michigan.apis.1385.s: This papyrus contains a fragment of the Acta Pauli
michigan.apis.1385.dt: second half of IIIrd century - first half of IVth century

michigan.apis.1386.s: Iliad 3.1-25. The single variant in l. 13 is a reminiscence

michigan.apis.1387.t: Narrative about the hypothesis of Temenidai
michigan.apis.1387.s: The narrative deals with a battle between the sons of Herakles and the Peloponnesians. Before the battle Temenos, the eldest of the Herakleidai, offered the kingdom to that one of his sons who gained most distinction in it. Success in the battle fell to the Heraklidai, and Archelaos the eldest was adjudged the most distinguished.;The narrative seems to go back to a hypothesis of the Temenidai, because it displays a remarkable overlap with fr. 107 of P.Oxy. XXVII 2455. In addition to this overlap, Luppe points to the occurence of participles and other expressions. But there is a diffreence as well: the repetition of words does not agree with the usual style, cf. l. 3, 4-5, 8 and 9.

michigan.apis.1388.t: Decision of a Iudex Datus in an Intestate Inheritance
michigan.apis.1388.s: Official copy of the decision taken by a centurion acting as judge in a dispute about the inheritance of an auxiliary soldier, who had died without having a testament
k: Vocontii; Cyrenaica; Falerna (tribus); Xoitana; [- - -]dium, Heliopolite nome

michigan.apis.1389.s: Soueris, daughter of Onnophris, granddaughter of Labesis, mother Soueris, acting with her husband, Orseus, son of Tryphon, as her guardian, divides her property equally between her two sons, Onnophris and Tephersais. The property consists of a house inherited from her father, a share of another house and court that has been purchased, and household goods and clothing. The sons have the responsibility of providing a fitting funeral for their mother. To her daughter, Thermouthis, Soueris has left the sum of sixty drachmas, perhaps in addition to dowry already received. This is probably to be a charge on the estate after the mother's death. All the other terms of the agreement has been lost.
michigan.apis.1389.luogo: Tebtunis, Polemon division, Arsinoite nome, province of Egypt (?)

michigan.apis.1390.s: This papyrus contains receipts for various garden taxes and surcharges, including the eight-drachma Dionysos libation tax. Figures given probably represent Ptolemaic copper drachmas, except those given for the eight-drachma Dionysos libation tax which is specified in the text as being paid in silver drachmas.

michigan.apis.1391.s: Ptolemaios, son of Ptolemaios, a former agoranomos, acknowledges that he has received from Onesimos, son of Amerimnos, a cook, 300 drachmas which Onesimos had obtained, possibly as an advance for wages due to him. The receipt ends with the usual statement that the advancer does not bring any charge against the receiver.

michigan.apis.1392.s: This papyrus contains a petition directed to the demosioi of Theadelphia by a certain Patron, son of Maron, who lives in the metropolis of the Arsinoite nome. Patron apparently had a house in Theadelphia and he submits the petition to report the situation to the police and to request that Chairemon give security to restrain him from further instances of illegal entry.
michigan.apis.1392.luogo: Theadelphia, Themistou meris, Arsinoite nome, province of Egypt

michigan.apis.1393.s: Private letter sent by Ptolemaios to his mother and sister, in which he answers various points in a letter he received from them, tells them of a four day episode spent with an irresponsible, impudent young man, somehow related to them, and complains a woman who treated him inconsiderably
michigan.apis.1393.sup: 1 + 2 papyri ; P.Mich. inv. 1341: 13 x 14.3 cm; P.Haun. II, 14: 12.5 x 13 cm; P.Haun. II, 15: 14.8 x 14 cm (total size: ca. 25.5 x 28.3 cm)

michigan.apis.1394.s: The text on this side of the papyrus is the upper portion of the first column of a roll devoted to a sitologos report. The sitologoi of the village Philopator also called of Theogenes here present an itemized journal of receipts of transportation charges on wheat moved from the granary to the harbour at Kerke. Neither the name nor the title of the official to whom the document was sent is recorded, but he was presumably the strategos (cf. P. Berl. Leihg. I, 1, introd.).

michigan.apis.1396.s: document in which Aurelius Sarapion acknowledges that he has sold two cows to Aurelius Ammonaspasis
michigan.apis.1396.luogo: Philadelphia, Herakleidou meris, Arsinoite nome, province of Egypt

michigan.apis.1397.s: A certain Aurelius Cornelius offers to lease from Aurelius Apollonius, honorably discharged soldier, two and one-half arouras of catoechic land grain land near Tanis, a village in the Arsinoite nome not far from the lessee's home town Philadelphia. The lease is to run for one year, at the comparatively low fixed rent of five artabas of wheat. Farm labor and dike maintenance are incumbent on the lessee, taxes and forced land assignments on the lessor. The latter signs the agreement of the offer in lines 23-24.
michigan.apis.1397.luogo: Philadelphia, Herakleidou meris, Arsinoite nome, province of Egypt

michigan.apis.1431.s: Recto contains five receipts forsyntaximon paid by three individuals: a. A shepherd, son of Mysthas and Aplonia from late in the reign of Nero; b. an unskilled laborer, Herakles, son of Pasion, grandson of Herakles, with a mother Thaesis, daughter of Nepheros, from year 13 of of Nero (= 66/67 A.D.). Nos. 4 and 5 (=col. I, lines 10-16; 17-20), dated to two different years early in the reign of Vespasian (line 10, note ad loc.); c. a workman, (no. 3 = col. III, lines 31-43); the receipt is for year 2 of Galba (= 68/69 A.D.).; he first column of the verso contains two receipts for beer tax (nos. 6 and 7). Second column begins with an additional receipt for beer tax (no. 9). The last receipt in the second column is also severely damaged (no. 10 = ll. 60-64), yet it too may be a receipt for beer tax.

michigan.apis.1432.s: This papyrus contains the lower part of a copy of a petition which is practically completely preserved in P. Mich. inv. 1440 (a subsequent copy composed, cf. palaeographical description): inv. 1436, lines 2-10 recur in inv. 1440, lines 11-17. In this petition Isidoros, son of Isidoros, from Sophthis in the Memphite nome, protests the illegal behaviour of Tryphon, the strategos of the Arsinoite nome. Through his agents, Tryphon appears to have forced Isidoros to make s sworn statement (cheirographia) regarding the sowing of seed grain land at Philadelphia. Although Isidoros submitted the cheirographia as directed (inv. 1440.16 = inv. 1436.8-9), he came to resent the compulsion put upon him by Tryphon and his agents, and to consider the imposition, because he was from Sophthis in the Memphite nome, which was Isidoros' idia, and where he was registered for tax purposes.
michigan.apis.1432.luogo: Philadelphia, Herakleidou meris, Arsinoite nome, province of Egypt (?)

michigan.apis.1442.s: Astronomical ephemeris for 467 A.D. covering parts of the first three months of the Egyptian year, Thoth, Phaophi and Hathyr. The numbering of the weeks, the Roman, Egyptian or Alexandrian, and lunar months; the daily position of the moon expressed by sign, degree, and minute, and the hour at which it passes from sign to sign; the daily position of the sun, Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Venus and Mercury; and designations of each day as a good, bad, or indifferent, doubtless based on astrological considerations such as the aspects of the heavenly bodies.

michigan.apis.1444.s: This official correspondence records the following events (in reverse chronological order, as was usual): a. A former gymnasiarch in the Arsinoite nome and a group, of unknown size, of diakritai ektheseon of the division of Themistes of this nome submitted a petition (lines 15 ff.) to the strategos of the division of Themistes and Polemon, Aelius Numisianus, probably with regard to the activities of the sitologoi of the Themistes. The date is lost; b. On August 14, 140 A.D. (Mesore 21, third year of Antoninus Pius), Aelius Numisianus forwarded a copy of the petition to Apol(l)inarios, strategos of the meris of Herakleides of the Arsinoite nome, apparently requesting that he look into the matter (lines 8-14); c. Promptly, on the following day (Aug. 15), Apollinarios sent copies of the petition and covering letter to his royal scribe, Sarapion, instructing him to deal with the problem (lines 2-7).
michigan.apis.1444.luogo: Meris of Herakleides, Arsinoite nome, province of Egypt

The endorsement by the prefect (3rd hand) shows that his request of a hearing of the case in front of the strategos of the name was granted.

These documents were of course intended to assist a judge in arriving at a decision favorable to an advocate's client; they are offered as precedents supporting the desired judgment.

michigan.apis.1482.s: Homer, Odyssey 23.8-16, 34-49 (om. 48). ;The text gives one previously unreported variant from the vulgate in l. 12; "EOUSAN"; vulg. "EONTA". The use of the feminine participle in place of the vulgate's masculine is the result of too specific interpretation of lines 11 and 12. At the beginning of 11, Penelope addresses the nurse directly. But the rest of 11 and all of 12 and 13 contain a general reflection on the power of the gods to affect men's wits, and so the masculine participle is used. But the Michigan text has taken 11-13 to refer specifically to the nurse; thus the use of the feminine. If the place were preserved, we would undoubtedly find "CHALIPHRONEOUSAN" for "CHALIPHRONEONTA" in l. 13.;40: "o]uk idon" rec. ou idon. The Michigan reading is vulgate. All codices and the lemma of sch. Q read "ouk". The vulgate ignores the digamma which begins "idon". Cf. P.Cornell XII (Il. 9.270).;41 "kteinomenon": The first letter of the word is broken, but there appears to be ink, unrelated to kappa, to its left, in the margin, of which only a very small portion is preserved. It appears to be a mark; the significance is unclear.
michigan.apis.1482.sup: 2 papyri ; a: 10.2 x 15.1 cm; fr. b 1.8 x 2.2. cm

michigan.apis.1483.s: Fragment of a geography of the Aeolian Islands (col. I) and of Sicily (col. II), mentioning also Kyme in Campania (Italy); it combined mythological geography (in part. the geography of the Odyssey) and an interest for natural (volcanic) phenomena, and gave distance figures betweenplaces

michigan.apis.1486.s: The document is a petition addressed to Harpokration, strategos of the Themistes and Polemon divisions of the Arsinoite nome, in 162 A.D. by Ptolemaios, son of Diodoros alias Dioskoros, a resident of Theadelphia.
michigan.apis.1486.luogo: Theadelphia, Themistou meris, Arsinoite nome, province of Egypt

michigan.apis.1487.s: In this text, formed as a letter, Isidoros orders Makarios to pay 300 myriads of denarii of silver to a certain Aion.

michigan.apis.1488.s: This letter is from the strategos of the Hermopolite nome (?) to the guardians of the Peace of the village of Mnachis. The addressees are to deliver the accused individuals, both of whom were chief men of a village (Mnachis)?
michigan.apis.1488.luogo: Mnachis, Hermopolite nome, middle Egypt, province of Egypt

michigan.apis.1489.s: The writer of this private letter anticipates a clash of jurisdiction with local officials over a piece of work of an unspecified nature for which a certain Heron, presumably a contractor, is providing the laborers. He instructs Chariton to keep a close eye on the undertaking and at the same time to warn off the demosioi as lacking authority over Heron.

michigan.apis.1490.s: This papyrus contains the beginning of a letter addressed to a landowner (geouchos). The sender, Apa Hor, reports on the activities of one Peter, an assistant (boethos) connected with the Oxyrhynchite village of Tholthis. We learn that Peter entered a hamlet (epoikion) belonging to the landowner and perpetrated an act described by the verb epiasen. At this point the sheet breaks off and leaves us in the dark about the sequel.
michigan.apis.1490.luogo: Oxyrhynchos, Oxyrhynchite nome, Middle Egypt, province of Egypt

michigan.apis.1491.t: Note to accompany gift of wine
michigan.apis.1491.s: Note in which a father donates one flagon of wine at the occasions of his son's wedding.

michigan.apis.1492.s: Letter sent by Plousia to Syros, with a message for another man; she expresses concerns for their well-being, at a time of trouble (polemos)

michigan.apis.1493.s: This papyrus appears to contain a hand-list of notes for a sermon on the cross in the tradition of the sermon De inventione sanctae crucis of Alexander Monachus (MG 87 III 4073 et sqq.). The text was perhaps meant to constitute an encomium to follow a discussion similar to that which precedes Alexander's encomium in De Inventione.

michigan.apis.1494.s: An urgent appeal from a son (or daughter?) to his/her father, asking him to come at once; otherwise the daily "hiding" which he/she fears from his/her overseers will force him/her to leave

michigan.apis.1495.s: Letter from Nemesion to his "brother" Tryphon, complaining that a lawsuit has been brought against him by a certain Papei, acting on behalf of the archimachairophoros
michigan.apis.1495.dt: (First half of the) Ist century A.D.
michigan.apis.1495.luogo: probably Philadelphia, Herakleidou meris, Arsinoite nome, province of Egypt

michigan.apis.1496.s: Achillas writes presumably to his wife Thaisous and his son Achilleus. The main part of the letter concerns a "dishonored" woman. This woman was probably travelling to Alexandria for a hearing with the prefect of Egypt, but the interest of Achillas, the author of the letter, is far from clear. The verso contains very faded traces of the address.

michigan.apis.1497.s: Letter from Psaeis, son of Apa Boreus, in which he informs his wife that he has sent her a number of household objects.

michigan.apis.1498.s: Letter sent to Herakles by Areskousa, who informs him of the excessive price requested from her for the care of a sow, and who asks him for some good cotton thread

michigan.apis.1499.t: Receipt (Certificate) for work performed for the penthemeral dyke corvȨe
michigan.apis.1499.s: Receipt (Certificate) for work performed on the embankments for the penthemeral dyke corvȨe
michigan.apis.1499.luogo: Theadelphia, Themistou meris, Arsinoite nome, province of Egypt

michigan.apis.1500.s: Private letter in which the author urges a certain Horion to bring the sekoma-measure.

michigan.apis.1501.s: End of a letter, requesting some unknown information

michigan.apis.1502.s: Letter concerned with some mainly agricultural business

michigan.apis.1503.s: This private letter is entirely concerned with a matter of business. The writer's attention is concentrated on the need of money to defray expenses and of papyrus for producing accounts, or a register of other official papers. The drift of the text suggests that he is a partner in a small firm of scribes, perhaps a family enterprise, specializing in such work.

michigan.apis.1504.s: This papyrus contains a letter from Lykarion to Tryphon, which appears to be that directive desired of the prefect by Isidoros in his petition (P. Mich. inv. 1440, 14-16 and Inv. 1436, 6-9).

michigan.apis.1505.s: this letter contains an original of a directive emanating from the office of the prefect. In this letter the prefect asks someone, whom he adressess as 'brother' (l. 8) and to whom he extends the bureaucratic courtesy of reciprocity (l. 9), to investigate Isidoros' claim of being from the Memphite nome (ll. 4-5). Scapula further delegates to the recipient of this letter the task of informing Tryphon that he is no longer to trouble Isidoros and is to return the cheirographia which Tryphon's agents took, should Isidoros' claims prove valid (l. 4-7).
michigan.apis.1505.luogo: Philadelphia, Herakleidou meris, Arsinoite nome, province of Egypt

michigan.apis.1506.s: Petition of a woman, concerning a dispute over an empty building lot, in the course of which some violence arose

michigan.apis.1507.s: The letter on this side of the papyrus concerns a grave difficulty experienced by the administrators of an estate at Toka. The local people had been ordered to do something about the cypress trees or cypress wood. The precise nature of the order is concealed by loss of text. The matter, however, seemed to them so serious that they had composed a letter to their landlord (geouchos). This they claimed had been suppressed by his agents on the spot. The writer advises his master, the landlord, to send them his decision.
michigan.apis.1507.luogo: Toka, Oxyrhynchite nome, Middle Egypt, province of Egypt

michigan.apis.1508.s: This papyrus contains the central portions of Iliad 18 (223-241).The text diverges in one instance from that of Allen (l. 5 = 227: "d'edaie" as opposed to "de daie").

michigan.apis.1509.s: Contract by which a priest leases for three years premises which had been used for keeping camels, and were now to be turned into a fowl-house
michigan.apis.1509.luogo: Oxyrhynchus, Oxyrhynchite nome, province of Egypt

michigan.apis.1511.s: Contains two summary tax accounts, one for Ptolemais (ll. 1-2) and one for Kerkesoucha (ll. 3-5).
michigan.apis.1511.luogo: probably Karanis, Herakleidou meris, Arsinoite nome, province of Egypt

michigan.apis.1512.s: Contract according to which Theokles, son of Euboulides, lends to Aristokles, son of Herakleides, the sum of 3 talents 780 drachmai for 13 months at 24 per cent interest, Megisto, the wife of aristokles being named as surety for her husband; the agreement concludes with the signalments of the contracting parties and surety. A note in the right margin seems to indicate that (after some time?) the affair had devolved to the sons of the contracting parties, only Megisto being still alive.
michigan.apis.1512.luogo: Philadelphia, Herakleidou meris, Arsinoite nome, Egypt
k: Philadelpheia (Philadelphia), Arsinoite nome; Makedon (tes epigones); Korinthios (tes epigones); Persine

michigan.apis.1513.s: Copy of official correspondence involving Septimius Zenus, the prefect of Egypt as well as the logistes of the Herakleopolite nome. This correspondence is spurred by a petition to the prefect, which was dealt with by local officials.
