princeton.apis.p562.luogo: Garrett Deposit 1926, no. II 225 in H. I. Bell's inventory
princeton.apis.p562.sup: 2 papyrus fragment; (a) 5.3 x 2.3 cm. (b) 7.1 x 2.6 cm

princeton.apis.p564.s: List of stolen property. List of articles left behind at her death by a certain Tloulla, and subsequently stolen by her husband, Paul. The inventory was prepared by her father doubtless as a preliminary step in obtaining redress on account of the loss of portion of her dowry

princeton.apis.p565.s: List of payments for various taxes
princeton.apis.p565.luogo: Given to Princeton University by the Egypt Exploration Society 1901

princeton.apis.p566.s: List of taxes. The entries consist of names in the nominative followed by "eis" with one or two names and the same four taxes
princeton.apis.p566.luogo: Given to Princeton University by the Egypt Exploration Society 1901

princeton.apis.p567.s: List of taxes. The entries consist of names in the nominative followed by "eis" with one or two names and the same four taxes
princeton.apis.p567.luogo: Given to Princeton University by the Egypt Exploration Society 1901

princeton.apis.p569.luogo: Garrett Deposit 1926, no. II 80 in H. I. Bell's inventory

princeton.apis.p570.s: Loan of 224 drachmas in silver made by Kollauthis to Nilus. Interest is at the rate of a drachma per mina per month

princeton.apis.p572.s: Aurelius Diogenes acknowledges to Aurelius Serenus also called Isidoros, son of Olympus, that he has receive a loan of 200 silver drachmas. In lieu of interest Serenus has the rightto inhabit the half part of a house belonging to Diogenes near the village of Philadelphia. If the loan is not repaid within a specific period, Serenus will have ownership of the half portion of the house

princeton.apis.p573.s: Aurelius Georgos, stable master, and his wife, Euphemia, daughter of Anoup, agree to repay a loan of four solidi when they receive advance payments on their salary for the fifteenth indiction

princeton.apis.p575.s: An acknowledgment of a loan of 100 drachmas and 2 artabas of wheat to be repaid in Pauni of the same year

princeton.apis.p576.s: An acknowledgment of a loan of 131 artabas of wheat negotiated between two brothers. It is clearly stated that the purpose of the loan is to defray the artabia on a plot cultivated by the borrower. the borrower agrees to include the transportation fees in the repayment of the loan. The loan is made on the written order or authorization of a third party

princeton.apis.p577.s: Loan of four artabas of wheat to be repaid at 50% interest. The loan is made by Aurelius Pekusus, son of Pausiris and Soeris, and his son Aurelius Petenouphis whose mother is Sintheus to Aurelius Theon, son of Didymus. Written in duplicate, on a single sheet in two columns, each in the same two hands
princeton.apis.p577.luogo: Given to Princeton University by the Egypt Exploration Society 1914-15

princeton.apis.p578.luogo: Given to Princeton University by the Egypt Exploration Society 1914-15

princeton.apis.p581.s: Message from a hegemon to Antonius, grammateus which refers to sending camels to Karanis and to wheat
princeton.apis.p581.luogo: Given to Princeton University by the Egypt Exploration Society, 1901

princeton.apis.p583.s: Nomination of Theon as sitologos with the nominator's whole property offered as surety

princeton.apis.p584.s: Order addressed by a decurion to the chiefs of the village of Teis, requesting them to send up for trial a certain Ammonios surnamed Alaker, who is accused by Ptollas
princeton.apis.p584.luogo: Given to Princeton University by the Egypt Exploration Society, 1901

princeton.apis.p585.s: Order from Joseph, councillor, to Phoibammon an oil manufacturer, instructing him to deliver two xestae of oil to the servants of Aeonis, a tractator. Five letters preceding the signature appear to have been written in shorthand

princeton.apis.p586.s: Order from Psenamounis to the baker, Atio, to pay 1,100 drachmas in silver for grain. The money is to be paid from funds in Atio's possession

princeton.apis.p587.s: Order from Dionysus to the sitologoi for payment of 12 3/4 artabas of wheat to Epimachus through Demetrius also called Theon. Dated in the 11th year of Antoninus
princeton.apis.p587.luogo: Given to Princeton University by the Egypt Exploration Society

princeton.apis.p588.s: Order from Sarapion to the sitologoi for payment of various amounts of wheat to various persons
princeton.apis.p588.luogo: Given to Princeton University by the Egypt Exploration Society

princeton.apis.p589.s: Order from Aphthonios to pay twenty talents to a wool merchant for some purpose connected with the landlord's house

princeton.apis.p591.s: Order from a speculator to the chief of police of the village of Taampemou to supply a donkey and a guard

princeton.apis.p592.s: Order for 19 jars of wine each holding 4 choes and 8 jars each holding 2 choes. Reference is made to an earlier shipment of 288 4-choes jars

princeton.apis.p595.s: Petition to an oikonomos from a basilikos georgos
princeton.apis.p595.luogo: Given to Princeton University in 1957 by Edmund H. Kase in memory of Professor Allan Chester Johnson

princeton.apis.p596.s: Petition. Mentions the name Zoilos. Préaux identifies this text as a letter rather than as a petition [CE 23 (1948), 199]

princeton.apis.p597.s: Petition from Thaesis, a tenant of a cleruchic allotment, for repayment of 293 artabas of wheat which she had depositied with Tesenouphis. A fragmentary subscription may have given the outcome of the trial

princeton.apis.p598.t: Petition to the Chief of Police
princeton.apis.p598.s: Petition addressed to Quintus Pacillus Euxinus, epistates, by Harthotes, son of Marreis, in which the writer reports the nocturnal intrusion of shepherds into his fields, resulting in the loss of half an aroura of hay, for which he seeks redress

princeton.apis.p601.s: Petition to Aurelius Severus deputy-epistategos from Aurelius Ptolemaios son of Sempronius son of Lucius. the father of a youth qualified to become an ephebus, complaining that his son's name had been omitted from the list which was annually prepared by the amphodogrammateus, and begging that the error might be rectified
princeton.apis.p601.luogo: Given to Princeton University by the Egypt Exploration Society, 1914-15

princeton.apis.p602.luogo: Garrett Deposit 1924, no. XIVb 68 in H. I. Bell's inventory
princeton.apis.p602.sup: 2 papyrus fragment; (a) 16.2 x 24 cm. (b) 11.7 x 7 cm

princeton.apis.p603.s: Beginning of a petition addressed to Flavius Dioskoros, a police official
princeton.apis.p603.luogo: Given to Princeton University by the Egypt Exploration Society, 1907

princeton.apis.p604.s: Beginning of a petition addressed to Flavius Asklepiades Hesychius which refers to a debtor and a fine incurred in a law suit
k: Flavius Asklepiades Hesychius, -- praeses of the Thebaid

princeton.apis.p605.t: Petition to the proximi of a City
princeton.apis.p605.s: Beginning of a petition to Flavius Sarapammon and Serenus, the proximi of a city, from Philoxenos concerning his complaint that, in the presence of seven witnesses, he has released a certain Akous, son of Apollo, but has not yet received in return the sum of 2 carats

princeton.apis.p606.s: Fragmentary account of some legal proceedings in which 50 pounds of gold were involved. Content unclear

princeton.apis.p607.s: Petition. Someone from the plaintiff's village had married a woman from another village and had become a leader in raids against his former villages. The petition seems to be an appeal to the headman of the village to restrain his people from their lawless acts. If no such action is taken, the plaintiffs will act for themselves, apparently without recourse to law or higher authority

princeton.apis.p610.s: Petition to the prefect Gaius Avidius Heliodorus (prefect 140-143 AD), from Marcus Valerius Gemellus, physician, seeking release from acting as supervisor of certain estates near thevillages of Bacchias and Hephaestias, confiscated by the government. He makes the claim on the grounds of ill health and the fact that he has supervised these estates for four years He a lso seeks exemption from other liturgies because of his profession
princeton.apis.p610.luogo: Given to Princeton University by the Egypt Exploration Society, 1901
k: Gaius Avidius Heliodorus, -- prefect of Egypt 140-143 AD

princeton.apis.p611.s: Petition to the prefect. Content is unclear, but in some way, the patria potestes of someone (the petitioner?) is in some way connected with the problem. Refers to a woman named Aurelia Isarion

princeton.apis.p612.s: Petition to Hermodoros, basilikogrammateus and acting strategos, from Didymos, a minor, complaining of fraud on the part of his mother, Matrina, in her capacity as his guardian. It is alleged that Matrina, after various acts of bad faith, had obtained possession of a deed belonging to Didymos and demanded in exchange for it a document absolving her from all claims in connection with the guardianship
princeton.apis.p612.luogo: Given to Princeton University by the Egypt Exploration Society

princeton.apis.p613.s: Opening lines of a petition addressed to Tiberius Claudius Sara[pion], who was, perhaps, a strategos, from Euporos Apete[ . Refers to a daughter of Euporos

princeton.apis.p614.s: Petition to the strategos of the Herakleides division of the Arsinoite nome in which the writer of the petition reports an accident involving severe injury to his brother. Although the details are uncertain, it appears that one of the brothers, Atammon, fell from a roof in the village of Kaminou, the accident having been in some way occasioned by an attack by Libyans. The injured man has received no medical attention and his brother petitions the strategos to take some action so that Atammon's life may be spared

princeton.apis.p615.s: Opening lines of a petition from Aurelia Asklatarion, also called Coprilla, to Aurelius Spartiates, also called Chairemon, strategos of the Hermopolite nome
k: Aurelius Spartiates, also called Chairemon, -- strategos of the Hermopolite nome
Aurelia Asklatarion, also called Coprilla, -- in P.Princ. II 38

princeton.apis.p616.s: Return of house property, submitted by Sambous, daughter of Pnepheros, son of Dionysios to the keepers of the property registers of the Arsinoite nome, the ex-gymnasiarchs Dios, also called Apollonios, and Herodes, also called Diogenes; Sambous' brother, Allothon(?) is acting for her in registering a half share in a house and courtyard
princeton.apis.p616.luogo: Given to Princeton University by the Egypt Exploration Society, 1901

princeton.apis.p617.s: Return of property for a half share in a house and courtyard submitted by Alexion to the keepers of the property registers of the Arsinoite nome, Dios and Herodes (see apis.p0616); the signature of Dios appears at the top in a different hand; dated in Mesore of the fifteenth year of Hadrian
princeton.apis.p617.luogo: Given to Princeton University by the Egypt Exploration Society, 1901

princeton.apis.p619.s: Receipt for payment of garden taxes for the year 145 AD. Paid by Athenarion the elder, daughter of Herodes

princeton.apis.p620.s: Receipt for 118 dr. paid for taxes on 26 1/2 arouras of katoikic land in the neighborhood of Pela in the allotment of Diodoros, son of Demokrates. Paid to Neilos and Sarapammon tax collectors, by Origeneia, daughter of Marcus [ ] Niger (?) and Demetria daughter of Sarapodoros. Origeneia is a citizen of Alexandria, as is her representative in the transaction Apollonios alias Didymos, son of Apollonios (?), grandson of Dioskoros. The land was ceded to Origeneia and Demetria by Tbekis, daughter of Pausiris and Kollauchis, from Pela

princeton.apis.p621.s: Customs house receipt for payment of the dues on three donkey loads (9 artabas) of orobos being exported through the customs house at Bacchias
princeton.apis.p621.luogo: Given to Princeton University by the Egypt Exploration Society, 1901

princeton.apis.p622.s: Customs house receipt for payment of the limen Mempheos on a small shipment of dates being exported through the customs house at Philadelphia

princeton.apis.p623.s: Receipt for 11 1/6 artabas of wheat, probably for phylakitikon and iatrikon. Dated Year 16 (of Euergetes) Phaophi 11
princeton.apis.p623.luogo: Given to Princeton University by the Egypt Exploration Society, 1907

princeton.apis.p624.s: Shipping receipt in which the kybernetes in command of three boats engaged in the transportation of grain to Alexandria, acknowledges to the sitologoi of Arsinoite Philadelphia the loading of 8627 1/2 artabas of wheat

princeton.apis.p625.s: For one artaba of wheat paid out from the deposit of Diogas, by the silologoi for the topos of Monimou; contains the signature of the recipient
princeton.apis.p625.luogo: Given to Princeton University by the Egypt Exploration Society, 1907

princeton.apis.p626.s: Receipt for twenty-eight artabas of wheat paid to the public officials
princeton.apis.p626.luogo: Given to Princeton University by the Egypt Exploration Society, 1907

princeton.apis.p627.s: Receipt for payment of sixty-five artabas of wheat paid out by the sitologoi of the eastern toparchy
princeton.apis.p627.luogo: Given to Princeton University by the Egypt Exploration Society, 1907

princeton.apis.p628.inv: Princ. inv. Garrett Deposit 124, Bell II 218 D
princeton.apis.p628.s: Receipt for one artaba of grain
princeton.apis.p628.luogo: Garrett Deposit 1924, no. II 218 in H. I. Bell's inventory

princeton.apis.p629.s: Receipt for grain paid to Eusebios, ordinarius. by Timotheos on behalf of Anelios, kybernetes

princeton.apis.p630.t: Receipt for Payment of a Debt
princeton.apis.p630.s: Receipt issued by Neilos, son of Mysthos, to Aretion Nasonos for payment of a debt

princeton.apis.p631.s: Taseus, daughter of Pekysis, with her father acting as guardian, acknowledges the receipt of 300 drachmas of silver and interest. Asklepiades acts as scribe. Recorded by Alexander in charge of the record office of the middle toparchy

princeton.apis.p632.s: Horos acknowledges to Ekysis the receipt of a sum which was owed to him by the latter. The transaction appears to cover various debts previously incurred by Ekysis

princeton.apis.p633.s: Chairemon, son of Sarapion, his mother being Taplutas, acknowledges that he has received from Tryphon son of Herakleides, the sum of 600 silver drachmas plus interest which was owed to him. The transaction took place before time, through the bank bank at the Serapeum at Oxyrhynchus, the officials involved being Phanias, ex chief priest and Ptolemaios, both described as the overseers associated with Audasius Paulinus
princeton.apis.p633.luogo: Given to Princeton University by the Egypt Exploration Society, 1914-15

princeton.apis.p634.s: Acknowledgment of receipt of 600 drachmas plus interest of a drachma per mina per month lent by Chr..ous, son(?) of Amois, his mother being Asklepia, to a man whose mother is Demetrous Both parties live in the hamlet of Dositheos
princeton.apis.p634.luogo: Given to Princeton University in 1957 by Edmund H. Kase in memory of Professor Allan Chester Johnson

princeton.apis.p635.s: Receipt for the repayment of a mixed loan of wheat and money lent to Aurelius Kollouthos by Aurelius Tithoes, son of Tithoes

princeton.apis.p636.s: Receipt dated by the eras of Oxyrhyhnchus, for three sextarii of oil. Received through Serenus, collector, by Makarios and Elias and Kamoul
princeton.apis.p636.luogo: Given to Princeton University by the Egypt Exploration Society

princeton.apis.p637.s: Receipt for payment of rent, partly in olyra, partly in a money equivalent of wheat, by two farmers. Land appears to be crown land. The protocol contains a mention of the association of the gods Adelphi with Alexander in the Alexandrian cult. Reference to the canephorus of Arsinoe is missing
princeton.apis.p637.luogo: Given to Princeton University by the Egypt Exploration Society, 1907

princeton.apis.p638.t: Receipt for the Repayment of Rent (?)
princeton.apis.p638.s: Receipt for payment of rent(?), with omologia formula. Written by Papontos son of Nekpheros to Socrates son of Apollonios

princeton.apis.p639.t: Receipts for Payment of Rent on Leased Land
princeton.apis.p639.s: The text is divided into two columns, in each of which a separate receipt is recorded. Both receipts are for payment of rent (ekphorion)made on a parcel of land situated near Tanis a small village a few miles south of Philadelphia. The land is part of a chleros. Aurelious Herakleides, ex-cosmete of Alexandria appears as lessor. The land was leased by Aurelius Patron, Aurelius Asoeis and Aurelius Atammon. The amount of rent paid in the first receipt is not stated, but in the second it is 656 1/2 artabas

princeton.apis.p640.s: Receipt for payments of wine made by Anoup and Johannes to Martyrios
princeton.apis.p640.luogo: Given to Princeton University by the Egypt Exploration Society, 1914-15

princeton.apis.p642.s: Receipt for 100 drachmas for the annona militum, paid by a high priest, Bitharion. The tax may have been paid to a female tax collector

princeton.apis.p643.s: Receipt for the brewing tax in the amount of eighteen drachmas for the month of Pachon paid by Petosiris, agent of Taembes. At the end are the signature of Dorion and a line of demotic
princeton.apis.p643.luogo: Given to Princeton University by the Egypt Exploration Society, 1907

princeton.apis.p645.s: Receipt for payment of 2 7/24 carats for tax, the demosia. Could refer to the land tax in particular or public taxes in general. Received by Kollouthos also called Stephanos

princeton.apis.p646.s: Receipt for 30 artabas of grain collected for land tax

princeton.apis.p647.s: Receipt for tax, the merismos. This and P.Princ. 91 were written by the same hand and issued to the same person, Makarios son of Kerekos(?), in different months of the same year presumably as installments for the tax

princeton.apis.p649.s: Receipt for nine(?) obols of copper paid for dike work
princeton.apis.p649.luogo: Given to Princeton University by the Egypt Exploration Society, 1901

princeton.apis.p650.s: Receipt for nine(?) obols of copper paid an unidentified tax
princeton.apis.p650.luogo: Given to Princeton University by the Egypt Exploration Society, 1901

princeton.apis.p651.s: Receipt for for various taxes, including dike work
princeton.apis.p651.luogo: Given to Princeton University by the Egypt Exploration Society, 1901

princeton.apis.p652.s: Receipt for one sixth of a solidus paid for poll tax

princeton.apis.p653.s: Receipt for 3 1/2 carats paid for poll tax paid by Dioskoros on behalf of Phoibammon

princeton.apis.p654.s: Three receipts for payment of twenty drachmas each from three brothers, Chairemon, Herakles(?) and Diodoros for poll tax. All have the same father, Chairemon; the mother of Herakles and Diodoros is Apia, Chairemon's mother being Diodora

princeton.apis.p655.s: Receipt for 20 drachmas, 10 obols received as poll tax from a resident of the Macedonian quarter of Arsinoe, Polios Horos, son of Pathermouthios, his mother being Taeus

princeton.apis.p656.s: Receipt for 44 drachmas paid in several installments for the poll tax

princeton.apis.p657.s: Receipt for 20 drachmas, 10 obols for the poll tax of the seventeenth year
princeton.apis.p657.luogo: Given to Princeton University by the Egypt Exploration Society, 1901

princeton.apis.p658.s: Receipt for 20 drachmaas, 10 obols for the poll tax paid by Zosimos
princeton.apis.p658.luogo: Given to Princeton University by the Egypt Exploration Society, 1901

princeton.apis.p659.s: Receipt for 12 drachmas, 1 1/2 obols, 2 chalci received in partial payment of the poll tax, together with smaller sums paid on various taxes

princeton.apis.p660.s: Receipt for 20 drachmas as payment for the tax imposed upon calves offered for sacrifice

princeton.apis.p661.s: Receipt for 60 drachmas, 2 obols, 2 chalci for payment of trades' tax. The trade for which the tax was paid is not specified. An additional payment of 3 drachmas, 3 obols is also recorded, evidently representing a subsequent installment of the same tax

princeton.apis.p663.s: Receipt for harbor tax for persons leaving the Fayum
princeton.apis.p663.luogo: Given to Princeton University by the Egypt Exploration Society

princeton.apis.p664.s: Receipt for three-sixteenths of an artaba of barley issued by the grain collectors. The barley may have been part of a special requisition destined for the army massed in Syria for Caracalla's war against Parthia

princeton.apis.p665.s: Account for payments of taxes listing names and amounts paid in money
princeton.apis.p665.sup: 2 papyrus fragments; 18 x 12 and 11 x 6 cm

princeton.apis.p668.inv: Princ. inv. Garrett Deposit 1924, Bell X 86 D
princeton.apis.p668.s: Receipt for tax for a 12th indiction. The recipient is a priest (presbyteros) and his name might have been Sonsneus
princeton.apis.p668.luogo: Garrett Deposit 1924, no. X 86 in H. I. Bell's inventory

princeton.apis.p669.luogo: Garrett Deposit 1926, no. II 95 in H. I. Bell's inventory

princeton.apis.p671.luogo: Garrett Deposit 1926, no. II 214 in H. I. Bell's inventory

princeton.apis.p672.s: Receipt for 3,000 drachmas from the public bank at Oxyrhynchus made out to Aurelia Sintotoe also called Alitarion. The managers of the bank are named as Aurelius Ptolmion, exegete, and Aurelius Hereaklianos also called Morion chief priest

princeton.apis.p673.luogo: Garrett Deposit 1926, no. II 218 in H. I. Bell's inventory

princeton.apis.p674.luogo: Given to Princeton University, in 1947 by Mrs. Charles A. Askren of Tacoma, Washington

princeton.apis.p675.s: Receipt. Dated 21st of an unknown month; content unclear
princeton.apis.p675.luogo: Garrett Deposit 1924, no. II 210 in H. I. Bell's inventory

princeton.apis.p678.s: Daybook of arrears for payments of a tax, probably the syntaximon. Dated in the eleventh year of an unnamed emperor, in all probability Tiberius. Each entry consists of a name, patronymic and an amount

princeton.apis.p679.inv: Princ. inv. Garrett Deposit 1924, Bell IX 13 A
princeton.apis.p679.s: Register for expenses or contributions listed by villages or epoikia. In each case the agent is the local steward (pronoetes) of the large estate
princeton.apis.p679.luogo: Garrett Deposit 1924, no. IX 13 in H. I. Bell's inventory

princeton.apis.p680.luogo: Garrett Deposit 1926, no. II 91 in H. I. Bell's inventory

princeton.apis.p681.luogo: Garrett Deposit 1924, no. in H. I. Bell's inventory

princeton.apis.p682.s: Land register which lists names and amounts of both crown and private land
princeton.apis.p682.sup: 2 papyrus fragments; (a) 12 x 30 cm. (b) 12 x 6 cm

princeton.apis.p683.s: Private account of parcels of land, arranged by cultivator, probably listing rents; the crops are barley, wheat and flax; these are the accounts of a large estate

princeton.apis.p685.s: Notice from Zenon o the agoranomos to register the sale of a house(?) sold for 700 silver drachmas or 52 talents 3,000 drachmas of copper; at the end, a docket
princeton.apis.p685.luogo: Given to Princeton University by the Egypt Exploration Society, 1901

princeton.apis.p686.s: Sale of a house and contents; the vendors, Serenus and Euphemia, acknowledge the receipt of the purchase price; each states a different amount, probably because each is acknowledging their share of the amount; the total is 21 solidi; Serenus signed himself in a crude hand, but Kollouthos wrote for Euphemia

princeton.apis.p687.s: Sale of property in Ibion Argaiou; includes the name Aurelius Harpokration
princeton.apis.p687.luogo: Given to Princeton University in 1957 by Edmund H. Kase in memory of Professor Allan Chester Johnson

princeton.apis.p688.s: Sale of the third part of a slave, Sarapos, aged fourteen
princeton.apis.p688.luogo: Given to Princeton University by the Egypt Exploration Society, 1901

princeton.apis.p689.s: Sale of a slave; the name Johannes is mentioned along with a reference to (his?) children

princeton.apis.p690.s: Register for payment of the syntaximon; entries are recorded daily and list name, patronymic and amount paid

princeton.apis.p691.s: Record of a single day's payments of the syntaximon; this fragment differs from the other associated Princeton tax registers in that the scribe, in giving the total of daily receipts, added up the payments for the syntaximon and then added the payments for the pig tax as well

princeton.apis.p692.s: Register for payment of the syntaximon; entries are recorded daily and list name, patronymic and amount paid

princeton.apis.p693.s: Register for payment of the syntaximon; entries are recorded daily and list name, patronymic and amount paid

princeton.apis.p694.s: Register for payment of the syntaximon; entries are recorded daily and list name, patronymic and amount paid

princeton.apis.p695.s: Register of payments for the syntaximon; entries contain a name, date and amount paid, in each case installments of 4 drachmas, or multiples of 4; a space of two lines was left under each name for the record of his payments, which were entered by a second clerk; the names are not arranged alphabetically and the record is probably that of a street or quarter of Philadelphia; there are twelve names in all; check marks are beside the five names of those who have paid in full

princeton.apis.p696.s: Tax register, possibly for the poll tax; entries consist of a name, patronymic and a payment in the amount of 45 drachmas, 2 obols, the combined total paid for the laographia and pig tax; the arrangement of the list is topographical and entries refer to estates; the register is a record of Philadelphians residing outside the village; two systems of checking are found a single stroke is drawn under the name at the left of the entry in most cases but in others a stroke resembling a quarter circle is found at the left of the name

princeton.apis.p700.s: Register of arrears owed for the syntaximon and the dike tax in years 19, 20 and 21 of Tiberius by taxpayers whose idia was Philadelphia, but who were currently away from the village

princeton.apis.p701.s: Two short columns written on the verso of a longer tax register (P.Princ. 3); register of arrears in payment of the poll tax for the 19, 20 and 21st years of Tiberius; another scribe used the bottom for a record which resembles the day books of the syntaximon (col. II)

princeton.apis.p702.s: Tax register; list of names with only the patronymics preserved; of the nineteen people on the list four pay 5 drachmas, eleven pay 6 drachmas and three pay 8 drachmas

princeton.apis.p704.s: Register. Short entries, possibly dates (eis b, eis d) follow groups of ca. 6 lines of text. On the verso are five short lines of what appear to be calculations
princeton.apis.p704.sup: 2 papyrus fragments; (a)11 x 8.9 cm., (b) 9.9 x 2.1 cm

princeton.apis.p705.s: Tax Register? Concerns some kind of assessment based on (landed?) property for taxation
princeton.apis.p705.sup: 1 papyrus fragment; (a) 15.8 x 17.3 cm. (b) 19.4 x 17.2 cm

princeton.apis.p706.s: Registration of live stock, sheep and goats, for the current year; addressed to the strategos of the Oxyrhynchite nome, whose name may be Chaereas; presented to the toparch Sarapion who functions in a similar capacity in P.Oxy, 351

yale.apis.0051860000.s: Letter from a large estate context, probably 6th century CE. The writer mentions sending a pronoetes and symmachos to the Oxyrhynchite village of Pthochis. He claims not to have received a response (perhaps to previous letters) and to be in need of an exemption (ἄφεμα). Letter closes with uncertain reference to a village headman (μείζων) and a symmachos. The only intact word in frag. B (χρεωστουμένους) indicates that the letter surely concerns a debt of some sort.
